## Statement

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]], [[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]]), let $M$ be a chosen $P$-graded type-1 quantum weight module with $E_i$ and $F_i$ locally nilpotent ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and fix $i\in I$. For $\mu\in P$ put
$$H_\mu:=\ker(E_i)\cap M_\mu,\qquad a_\mu:=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle .$$
Then:

(i) $H_\mu=0$ whenever $a_\mu<0$;

(ii) if $a_\mu\ge0$, then $F_i^{(n)}:H_\mu\to M_{\mu-n\alpha_i}$ is injective for $0\le n\le a_\mu$ and is the zero map for $n>a_\mu$;

(iii) every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique finite **admissible decomposition** $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ and $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$;

(iv) consequently $M_\lambda$ is the internal direct sum of the nonzero admissible string spaces $F_i^{(n)}H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$.

Coefficients beyond a string's bottom are specified to be zero; arbitrary killed coefficients at the top are not allowed. No finite-dimensionality of $M$ or of its weight spaces, no bounded support, no uniform nilpotence and no choice principle is assumed; $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the integer pairing of the datum ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]) and $F_i^{(n)}$ is the divided power of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$, a chosen $P$-graded type-1 quantum weight module $M$ on which $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent, and $H_\mu=\ker(E_i)\cap M_\mu$, $a_\mu=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

[F1] $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$ with $K_h$ acting on $M_\mu$ by $q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$, $E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i}$ and $F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}$ for every $\mu$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$; $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

[F2] $a_{ii}=2$, so $\langle\alpha_i,h_i\rangle=2$ in the row convention; with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, the element $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$ acts on $M_\mu$ by the scalar $q_i^{a_\mu}$, and $E_i$ raises and $F_i$ lowers $a_\mu$ by $2$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]], [F1]).

[F3] $[m]_i=(q_i^m-q_i^{-m})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ for integer $m$, with $[0]_i=0$, $[1]_i=1$, $x^{(m)}=x^m/[m]_i!$ for $m\ge0$, and $[m]_i=0$ exactly when $m=0$, because $q_i$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

[F4] In the rank-one subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ one has $K_iE_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^2E_i$, $K_iF_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2}F_i$, $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, the identity $F_iF_i^{(b)}=[b+1]_iF_i^{(b+1)}$ for $b\ge0$, and the divided-power commutation formula: for $b\ge1$, with $\Theta_{i,b}:=(q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b})^{-1}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1})$, one has $E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+F_i^{(b-1)}\Theta_{i,b}$; iterating it, $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ is a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ with $0\le t\le\min(a,b)$ and coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]], parts (i)-(ii)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct. Reduce each vector to a finite-dimensional rank-one module, classify its simple factors by the Casimir, split the module by the generalized eigenspaces of the Casimir, and read off injectivity, existence and uniqueness of the string expansion; all arguments are finite and choice-free.

1.1 Finite-dimensional reduction. Let $u\in M_\lambda$. Choose $N\ge0$ with $E_i^Nu=0$ and set $W:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}\{F_i^{(a)}E_i^bu:0\le b<N,\ a\ge0\}$. Then $W$ is finite-dimensional: for each of the finitely many $b<N$ the local nilpotence of $F_i$ gives an integer $A_b$ with $F_i^{A_b}E_i^bu=0$, so the span of the vectors $F_i^{(a)}E_i^bu$, $a\ge0$, is already spanned by the finitely many vectors with $a<A_b$. [given, F1]

1.2 The commutation scalar. Let $v$ be a weight vector with $E_iv=0$ and $K_iv=q_i^av$, where $a=\langle\mathrm{wt}(v),h_i\rangle$. For $b\ge1$ the formula of [F4] gives $E_iF_i^{(b)}v=F_i^{(b-1)}\Theta_{i,b}v$, and $\Theta_{i,b}$ acts on $v$ by the scalar $(q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b})^{-1}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q_i^{-2s}q_i^{a}-q_i^{2s}q_i^{-a})=[a-b+1]_i$ by the finite geometric-sum identities; hence $E_iF_i^{(b)}v=[a-b+1]_iF_i^{(b-1)}v$. [F3, F4, algebra]

1.3 The Casimir. Put $\varphi(K_i):=(q_iK_i+q_i^{-1}K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})^2$ and $C:=F_iE_i+\varphi(K_i)\in A_i$. Then $C$ is central in $A_i$: from $K_iE_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^2E_i$ and $K_iF_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2}F_i$ one computes $\varphi(q_i^{2}K_i)-\varphi(K_i)=(q_i^{2}K_i-q_i^{-2}K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ and hence $[\varphi(K_i),E_i]=E_i(\varphi(q_i^2K_i)-\varphi(K_i))=(K_i-K_i^{-1})E_i/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=-[F_iE_i,E_i]$, while $\varphi(q_i^{-2}K_i)-\varphi(K_i)=-(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ gives $[\varphi(K_i),F_i]=-F_i(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=-[F_iE_i,F_i]$; so $[C,E_i]=[C,F_i]=0$, and $C$ commutes with $K_i^{\pm1}$ visibly. Moreover $C$ acts on every weight vector $v$ with $E_iv=0$ and $K_iv=q_i^av$ by the scalar $c_a:=\varphi(q_i^a)=(q_i^{a+1}+q_i^{-a-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})^2$. [F4, algebra]

2.1 The scalars $c_a$ for $a\ge0$ are pairwise distinct: if $c_a=c_b$ with $a,b\ge0$, then $q_i^{a+1}+q_i^{-a-1}=q_i^{b+1}+q_i^{-b-1}$, that is $(q_i^{a+1}-q_i^{b+1})(1-q_i^{-(a+b+2)})=0$; as $q_i$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $q_i^m=1$ forces $m=0$, so the second factor is nonzero and $q_i^{a+1}=q_i^{b+1}$ gives $a=b$. [F3, step 1.3, algebra]

2.2 $W$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-submodule on which $E_i$ and $F_i$ are nilpotent and $K_i$ is diagonalisable with eigenvalues in $q_i^{\mathbb Z}$. Indeed $F_iF_i^{(a)}=[a+1]_iF_i^{(a+1)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2a}F_i^{(a)}$ show that $F_i$ and $K_i$ preserve $W$, and for $a\ge1$ the commutation formula of [F4] gives $E_iF_i^{(a)}E_i^bu=F_i^{(a)}E_i^{b+1}u+\Theta_{i,a}F_i^{(a-1)}E_i^bu$, where $\Theta_{i,a}$ acts on the weight vector $E_i^bu$ by a scalar; for $b+1<N$ both terms lie in $W$, and for $b+1=N$ the first term is $F_i^{(a)}E_i^Nu=0$, so $E_i$ preserves $W$. Nilpotence is inherited from local nilpotence on the finite-dimensional $W$, and diagonalisability with the eigenvalue form from [F1] and [F2]. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Claims (i) and (ii). Let $0\ne v\in H_\mu$. By steps 1.1 and 2.2 applied with $N=1$, the span $W_v$ of $F_i^{(a)}v$, $a\ge0$, is a finite-dimensional module with $F_i$ nilpotent, so there is a minimal $t\ge1$ with $F_i^{(t)}v=0$, and $F_i^{(t-1)}v\ne0$. Step 1.2 gives $0=E_iF_i^{(t)}v=[a_\mu-t+1]_iF_i^{(t-1)}v$, hence $[a_\mu-t+1]_i=0$, which by [F3] means $a_\mu-t+1=0$, that is $t=a_\mu+1\ge1$. Thus $a_\mu\ge0$, and $F_i^{(n)}v\ne0$ for $0\le n\le a_\mu$ while $F_i^{(n)}v=F_i^{(n-a_\mu-1)}F_i^{(a_\mu+1)}v=0$ for $n>a_\mu$. As $v$ was an arbitrary nonzero element of $H_\mu$, this proves $H_\mu=0$ for $a_\mu<0$ and the injectivity and vanishing clauses for $F_i^{(n)}$ on $H_\mu$. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.2]

4.1 Simple factors. Let $S$ be a simple subquotient of a finite-dimensional type-1 $A_i$-module on which $E_i$ is nilpotent. Then $S$ contains a nonzero weight vector $v$ with $E_iv=0$: choose $0\ne w\in S$, let $m\ge1$ be minimal with $E_i^mw=0$ and put $v_0:=E_i^{m-1}w\ne0$; decomposing $v_0$ into weight components and using that $E_i$ preserves weights, some nonzero weight component $v$ satisfies $E_iv=0$. With $a:=\langle\mathrm{wt}(v),h_i\rangle$, step 3.1 gives $a\ge0$, $F_i^{(a)}v\ne0$ and $F_i^{(a+1)}v=0$. The span of $v,F_iv,\dots,F_i^{(a)}v$ is a nonzero $A_i$-submodule by the formulas of steps 1.2 and 2.2 together with $[0]_i=0$, so it equals the simple module $S$; these $a+1$ vectors have distinct weights, whence $\dim S=a+1$ and $C$ acts on $S$ by the scalar $c_a$ of step 1.3. [F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 Generalized-eigenspace splitting. Let $W$ be as in steps 1.1-2.2. Since $C$ is central in $A_i$, it preserves $A_i$-submodules and acts on each simple factor of $W$ by the scalar $c_a$ with $a\ge0$ from step 4.1. The characteristic polynomial of $C$ on $W$ therefore splits with roots among the pairwise distinct scalars $c_a$ of step 2.1, and the generalized eigenspaces $W[a]:=\ker(C-c_a)^{m}\cap W$ are $A_i$-submodules with $W=\bigoplus_aW[a]$. Every composition factor of $W[a]$ has highest label $a$: a factor of label $b\ne a$, $b\ge0$, would make $C-c_b$ non-invertible on $W[a]$, whereas $C-c_b$ is invertible on the generalized eigenspace of the distinct scalar $c_a$. [step 1.3, step 2.1, step 4.1]

6.1 Blocks. Fix $a\ge0$ with $W[a]\ne0$ and let $r:=\dim W[a]/(a+1)$, the number of composition factors of $W[a]$ counted with multiplicity. Each factor has by step 4.1 a weight-space decomposition into one-dimensional spaces of $K_i$-eigenvalues $q_i^{a},q_i^{a-2},\dots,q_i^{-a}$; hence the weight space of eigenvalue $q_i^{a-2n}$ has dimension $r$ for $0\le n\le a$, and $W[a]$ has no weight of eigenvalue $q_i^{m}$ with $m>a$. In particular $k:=\dim W[a]_{a}=r$, $\dim W[a]=k(a+1)$, and $E_i$ kills the top weight space $W[a]_{a}$ because it would raise the eigenvalue to $q_i^{a+2}$. [step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 String splitting of a block. For $w\in W[a]_{a}$ and $0\le n\le a$ one has $F_i^{(n)}w\ne0$: if $F_i^{(n)}w=0$ for some minimal $n\ge1$, then $F_i^{(n-1)}w\ne0$ and step 1.2 gives $0=E_iF_i^{(n)}w=[a-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}w$, forcing $n=a+1>a$ by [F3]. Hence each $N_n:=F_i^{(n)}W[a]_{a}$, $0\le n\le a$, has dimension $k$, and the $N_n$ lie in the distinct weight spaces of eigenvalues $q_i^{a-2n}$, so they are independent; their sum is $A_i$-stable because $E_iF_i^{(n)}w=[a-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}w$ and $F_iF_i^{(n)}w=[n+1]_iF_i^{(n+1)}w$ for $w\in W[a]_a$; being a submodule of dimension $k(a+1)=\dim W[a]$, the sum equals $W[a]$. [F3, step 1.2, step 6.1]

8.1 Existence. Let $u\in M_\lambda$ be homogeneous and let $W$ be the finite-dimensional reduction of steps 1.1-2.2, which contains $u$ and splits as $W=\bigoplus_aW[a]=\bigoplus_a\bigoplus_{n=0}^{a}F_i^{(n)}W[a]_{a}$ by steps 5.1-7.1. A summand $F_i^{(n)}W[a]_{a}$ lies in weight $\lambda$ exactly when $a-2n=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$, and then $W[a]_{a}\subseteq M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ with $E_i$ killing it, so it is contained in $H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$. Collecting, for each $n\ge0$, the top vectors of all blocks with $a=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle+2n$ into $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ gives $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$; here $u_n\ne0$ only when $0\le n\le a=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle+2n$, which is exactly the admissibility condition $n\le\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. For a general $u\in M_\lambda$, apply this to the finitely many nonzero homogeneous components of $u$ and add. [step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, algebra]

9.1 Uniqueness. Suppose $\sum_{n=0}^{N}F_i^{(n)}u_n=0$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ admissible and $u_N\ne0$. By [F4], $E_i^{N}F_i^{(n)}$ is a finite sum of terms $F_i^{(n-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{N-t}$ with $0\le t\le n$; for $n<N$ every $t\le n$ satisfies $N-t\ge N-n\ge1$, so each term kills $u_n$ (as $E_iu_n=0$), while for $n=N$ only $t=N$ survives and, by iterating step 1.2, $E_i^{N}F_i^{(N)}u_N=\bigl(\prod_{t=1}^{N}[a_N-t+1]_i\bigr)u_N$ with $a_N=\langle\lambda+N\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Admissibility gives $a_N\ge N$, so $a_N-t+1\ge1$ for $1\le t\le N$ and the product is nonzero by [F3]. Hence $0=E_i^{N}0=\bigl(\prod_{t=1}^{N}[a_N-t+1]_i\bigr)u_N$ forces $u_N=0$, a contradiction. [F3, F4, step 1.2, step 8.1]

10.1 Direct sum. By step 3.1(ii) applied to $H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$, the map $F_i^{(n)}$ on $H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ is injective for $n\le\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$ and zero otherwise. Steps 8.1 and 9.1 say that every $u\in M_\lambda$ is a unique sum of vectors from the nonzero spaces $F_i^{(n)}H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$, which is exactly the statement that $M_\lambda$ is their internal direct sum. All selections in the argument were among finitely many vectors or finitely many scalars, so no choice principle is used. [step 3.1, step 8.1, step 9.1] ∎

1.1 Finite-dimensional reduction. Let $u\in M_\lambda$. Choose $N\ge0$ with $E_i^Nu=0$ and set $W:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}\{F_i^{(a)}E_i^bu:0\le b<N,\ a\ge0\}$. Then $W$ is finite-dimensional: for each of the finitely many $b<N$ the local nilpotence of $F_i$ gives an integer $A_b$ with $F_i^{A_b}E_i^bu=0$, so the span of the vectors $F_i^{(a)}E_i^bu$, $a\ge0$, is already spanned by the finitely many vectors with $a<A_b$. [given, F1]

1.2 The commutation scalar. Let $v$ be a weight vector with $E_iv=0$ and $K_iv=q_i^av$, where $a=\langle\mathrm{wt}(v),h_i\rangle$. For $b\ge1$ the formula of [F4] gives $E_iF_i^{(b)}v=F_i^{(b-1)}\Theta_{i,b}v$, and $\Theta_{i,b}$ acts on $v$ by the scalar $(q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b})^{-1}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q_i^{-2s}q_i^{a}-q_i^{2s}q_i^{-a})=[a-b+1]_i$ by the finite geometric-sum identities; hence $E_iF_i^{(b)}v=[a-b+1]_iF_i^{(b-1)}v$. [F3, F4, algebra]

1.3 The Casimir. Put $\varphi(K_i):=(q_iK_i+q_i^{-1}K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})^2$ and $C:=F_iE_i+\varphi(K_i)\in A_i$. Then $C$ is central in $A_i$: from $K_iE_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^2E_i$ and $K_iF_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2}F_i$ one computes $\varphi(q_i^{2}K_i)-\varphi(K_i)=(q_i^{2}K_i-q_i^{-2}K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ and hence $[\varphi(K_i),E_i]=E_i(\varphi(q_i^2K_i)-\varphi(K_i))=(K_i-K_i^{-1})E_i/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=-[F_iE_i,E_i]$, while $\varphi(q_i^{-2}K_i)-\varphi(K_i)=-(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ gives $[\varphi(K_i),F_i]=-F_i(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=-[F_iE_i,F_i]$; so $[C,E_i]=[C,F_i]=0$, and $C$ commutes with $K_i^{\pm1}$ visibly. Moreover $C$ acts on every weight vector $v$ with $E_iv=0$ and $K_iv=q_i^av$ by the scalar $c_a:=\varphi(q_i^a)=(q_i^{a+1}+q_i^{-a-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})^2$. [F4, algebra]

2.1 The scalars $c_a$ for $a\ge0$ are pairwise distinct: if $c_a=c_b$ with $a,b\ge0$, then $q_i^{a+1}+q_i^{-a-1}=q_i^{b+1}+q_i^{-b-1}$, that is $(q_i^{a+1}-q_i^{b+1})(1-q_i^{-(a+b+2)})=0$; as $q_i$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $q_i^m=1$ forces $m=0$, so the second factor is nonzero and $q_i^{a+1}=q_i^{b+1}$ gives $a=b$. [F3, step 1.3, algebra]

2.2 $W$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-submodule on which $E_i$ and $F_i$ are nilpotent and $K_i$ is diagonalisable with eigenvalues in $q_i^{\mathbb Z}$. Indeed $F_iF_i^{(a)}=[a+1]_iF_i^{(a+1)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2a}F_i^{(a)}$ show that $F_i$ and $K_i$ preserve $W$, and for $a\ge1$ the commutation formula of [F4] gives $E_iF_i^{(a)}E_i^bu=F_i^{(a)}E_i^{b+1}u+F_i^{(a-1)}\Theta_{i,a}E_i^bu$, where $\Theta_{i,a}$ acts on the weight vector $E_i^bu$ by a scalar; for $b+1<N$ both terms lie in $W$, and for $b+1=N$ the first term is $F_i^{(a)}E_i^Nu=0$, so $E_i$ preserves $W$. Nilpotence is inherited from local nilpotence on the finite-dimensional $W$, and diagonalisability with the eigenvalue form from [F1] and [F2]. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 Claims (i) and (ii). Let $0\ne v\in H_\mu$. By steps 1.1 and 2.2 applied with $N=1$, the span $W_v$ of $F_i^{(a)}v$, $a\ge0$, is a finite-dimensional module with $F_i$ nilpotent, so there is a minimal $t\ge1$ with $F_i^{(t)}v=0$, and $F_i^{(t-1)}v\ne0$. Step 1.2 gives $0=E_iF_i^{(t)}v=[a_\mu-t+1]_iF_i^{(t-1)}v$, hence $[a_\mu-t+1]_i=0$, which by [F3] means $a_\mu-t+1=0$, that is $t=a_\mu+1\ge1$. Thus $a_\mu\ge0$, and $F_i^{(n)}v\ne0$ for $0\le n\le a_\mu$ while $F_i^{(n)}v=F_i^{(n-a_\mu-1)}F_i^{(a_\mu+1)}v=0$ for $n>a_\mu$. As $v$ was an arbitrary nonzero element of $H_\mu$, this proves $H_\mu=0$ for $a_\mu<0$ and the injectivity and vanishing clauses for $F_i^{(n)}$ on $H_\mu$. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.2]

4.1 Simple factors. Let $S$ be a simple subquotient of a finite-dimensional type-1 $A_i$-module on which $E_i$ is nilpotent. Then $S$ contains a nonzero weight vector $v$ with $E_iv=0$: choose $0\ne w\in S$, let $m\ge1$ be minimal with $E_i^mw=0$ and put $v_0:=E_i^{m-1}w\ne0$; decomposing $v_0$ into weight components and using that $E_i$ preserves weights, some nonzero weight component $v$ satisfies $E_iv=0$. With $a:=\langle\mathrm{wt}(v),h_i\rangle$, step 3.1 gives $a\ge0$, $F_i^{(a)}v\ne0$ and $F_i^{(a+1)}v=0$. The span of $v,F_iv,\dots,F_i^{(a)}v$ is a nonzero $A_i$-submodule by the formulas of steps 1.2 and 2.2 together with $[0]_i=0$, so it equals the simple module $S$; these $a+1$ vectors have distinct weights, whence $\dim S=a+1$ and $C$ acts on $S$ by the scalar $c_a$ of step 1.3. [F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 Generalized-eigenspace splitting. Let $W$ be as in steps 1.1-2.2. Since $C$ is central in $A_i$, it preserves $A_i$-submodules and acts on each simple factor of $W$ by the scalar $c_a$ with $a\ge0$ from step 4.1. The characteristic polynomial of $C$ on $W$ therefore splits with roots among the pairwise distinct scalars $c_a$ of step 2.1, and the generalized eigenspaces $W[a]:=\ker(C-c_a)^{m}\cap W$ are $A_i$-submodules with $W=\bigoplus_aW[a]$. Every composition factor of $W[a]$ has highest label $a$: a factor of label $b\ne a$, $b\ge0$, would make $C-c_b$ non-invertible on $W[a]$, whereas $C-c_b$ is invertible on the generalized eigenspace of the distinct scalar $c_a$. [step 1.3, step 2.1, step 4.1]

6.1 Blocks. Fix $a\ge0$ with $W[a]\ne0$ and let $r:=\dim W[a]/(a+1)$, the number of composition factors of $W[a]$ counted with multiplicity. Each factor has by step 4.1 a weight-space decomposition into one-dimensional spaces of $K_i$-eigenvalues $q_i^{a},q_i^{a-2},\dots,q_i^{-a}$; hence the weight space of eigenvalue $q_i^{a-2n}$ has dimension $r$ for $0\le n\le a$, and $W[a]$ has no weight of eigenvalue $q_i^{m}$ with $m>a$. In particular $k:=\dim W[a]_{a}=r$, $\dim W[a]=k(a+1)$, and $E_i$ kills the top weight space $W[a]_{a}$ because it would raise the eigenvalue to $q_i^{a+2}$. [step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 String splitting of a block. For $w\in W[a]_{a}$ and $0\le n\le a$ one has $F_i^{(n)}w\ne0$: if $F_i^{(n)}w=0$ for some minimal $n\ge1$, then $F_i^{(n-1)}w\ne0$ and step 1.2 gives $0=E_iF_i^{(n)}w=[a-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}w$, forcing $n=a+1>a$ by [F3]. Hence each $N_n:=F_i^{(n)}W[a]_{a}$, $0\le n\le a$, has dimension $k$, and the $N_n$ lie in the distinct weight spaces of eigenvalues $q_i^{a-2n}$, so they are independent; their sum is $A_i$-stable because $E_iF_i^{(n)}w=[a-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}w$ and $F_iF_i^{(n)}w=[n+1]_iF_i^{(n+1)}w$ for $w\in W[a]_a$; being a submodule of dimension $k(a+1)=\dim W[a]$, the sum equals $W[a]$. [F3, step 1.2, step 6.1]

8.1 Existence. Let $u\in M_\lambda$ be homogeneous and let $W$ be the finite-dimensional reduction of steps 1.1-2.2, which contains $u$ and splits as $W=\bigoplus_aW[a]=\bigoplus_a\bigoplus_{n=0}^{a}F_i^{(n)}W[a]_{a}$ by steps 5.1-7.1. A summand $F_i^{(n)}W[a]_{a}$ lies in weight $\lambda$ exactly when $a-2n=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$, and then $W[a]_{a}\subseteq M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ with $E_i$ killing it, so it is contained in $H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$. Collecting, for each $n\ge0$, the top vectors of all blocks with $a=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle+2n$ into $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ gives $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$; here $u_n\ne0$ only when $0\le n\le a=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle+2n$, which is exactly the admissibility condition $n\le\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. For a general $u\in M_\lambda$, apply this to the finitely many nonzero homogeneous components of $u$ and add. [step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, algebra]

9.1 Uniqueness. Suppose $\sum_{n=0}^{N}F_i^{(n)}u_n=0$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ admissible and $u_N\ne0$. By [F4], $E_i^{N}F_i^{(n)}$ is a finite sum of terms $F_i^{(n-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{N-t}$ with $0\le t\le n$; for $n<N$ every $t\le n$ satisfies $N-t\ge N-n\ge1$, so each term kills $u_n$ (as $E_iu_n=0$), while for $n=N$ only $t=N$ survives and, by iterating step 1.2, $E_i^{N}F_i^{(N)}u_N=\bigl(\prod_{t=1}^{N}[a_N-t+1]_i\bigr)u_N$ with $a_N=\langle\lambda+N\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Admissibility gives $a_N\ge N$, so $a_N-t+1\ge1$ for $1\le t\le N$ and the product is nonzero by [F3]. Hence $0=E_i^{N}0=\bigl(\prod_{t=1}^{N}[a_N-t+1]_i\bigr)u_N$ forces $u_N=0$, a contradiction. [F3, F4, step 1.2, step 8.1]

10.1 Direct sum. By step 3.1(ii) applied to $H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$, the map $F_i^{(n)}$ on $H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ is injective for $n\le\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$ and zero otherwise. Steps 8.1 and 9.1 say that every $u\in M_\lambda$ is a unique sum of vectors from the nonzero spaces $F_i^{(n)}H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$, which is exactly the statement that $M_\lambda$ is their internal direct sum. All selections in the argument were among finitely many vectors or finitely many scalars, so no choice principle is used. [step 3.1, step 8.1, step 9.1] ∎

## Definition

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_n)\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The negative-half counterpart of these operators, where the infinite string has no bottom and only the lower-string relation survives, is the skew-derivation pair of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]; it is not used here.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$, an index $i$, and for every $u\in M_\lambda$ its unique admissible decomposition $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$.

[F1] $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$ with $K_h$ acting on $M_\mu$ by $q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$, $E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i}$, $F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}$, and $E_i,F_i$ locally nilpotent; a nonzero element of $H_\mu$ has $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and $F_i^{(n)}$ is injective on $H_\mu$ for $0\le n\le\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$ and zero for $n>\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$, with $h_i$ the simple coroot of the datum ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]], [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

[F2] The decomposition of [F1] is unique and $M_\lambda$ is the internal direct sum of the nonzero spaces $F_i^{(n)}H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$; in particular the coefficient $u_n$ and the position of each string are well defined ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

[F3] Divided powers satisfy $F_iF_i^{(n)}=[n+1]_iF_i^{(n+1)}$ and $E_iF_i^{(n)}w=[a-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}w$ for $w\in H_\mu$ with $a=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$; the module $L_i(2)$ of dimension $3$ has a highest vector $v$ with $F_iv=[1]_iv_1$, $F_iv_1=[2]_iv_2$, $F_iv_2=0$, and $[2]_i=q_i+q_i^{-1}\neq1$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]], parts (ii)-(iii), [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct. All operators are read off the unique string decomposition string by string.

1.1 Linearity and weights. On a string position $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ put $\tilde e_i(F_i^{(n)}u_n):=F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ for $n\ge1$ and $0$ for $n=0$, and $\tilde f_i(F_i^{(n)}u_n):=F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$. By [F2] every $u$ is a unique sum of such positions inside its decomposition, so these prescriptions define linear maps on $M$; the shifted vectors lie in $M_{\lambda+\alpha_i}$ and $M_{\lambda-\alpha_i}$ respectively, since $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n\in M_{\lambda+\alpha_i}$ and $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n\in M_{\lambda-\alpha_i}$ by [F1]. [F1, F2]

2.1 The top projection. Writing $p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0$ gives a well-defined linear idempotent by [F2]. For $u=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}u_n$ one has $\tilde f_i\tilde e_iu=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ by step 1.1, hence $u-\tilde f_i\tilde e_iu=u_0=p_{\mathrm{top}}u$; equivalently $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}}$, and on each position with $n\ge1$ the composition $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i$ is the identity. [step 1.1, F2]

2.2 The bottom projection. If $n\ge\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$, then $n$ equals that length by [F1], and $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n=0$ because $F_i^{(n)}$ is zero beyond the string length; thus $\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n<\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$, which is the admissible decomposition of $\tilde f_iu$ (its $m$-th top coefficient is $u_{m-1}$ for $m\ge1$). Applying step 1.1 to this decomposition, $\tilde e_i\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n<\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n$, so $u-\tilde e_i\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n=p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u$; in particular on each position that is not a bottom the composition $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i$ is the identity. [F1, step 1.1, F2]

2.3 Kernels. For $u=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}u_n$, step 1.1 gives $\tilde e_iu=0$ exactly when $u_n=0$ for all $n\ge1$, that is $u=u_0\in H_\lambda$. On the other hand [F3] gives $E_iu=\sum_{n\ge1}[a_n-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ with $a_n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$; here $a_n-n+1\ge1$ for $n\le a_n$ by admissibility and the term vanishes for $n>a_n$, so $E_iu=0$ exactly when $u_n=0$ for all $n\ge1$ as well; hence $\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i$. Likewise $\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n<a_n}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n=0$ exactly when $u_n=0$ for all $n<a_n$, and $F_iu=\sum_{n<a_n}[n+1]_iF_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ vanishes exactly then because $[n+1]_i\neq0$; hence $\ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i$. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

2.4 Agreement on the kernels. If $u\in\ker E_i$ then $u=u_0$ by [F2], so $\tilde f_iu=F_iu_0=F_iu$; if $u\in\ker F_i$ then every nonzero coefficient $u_n$ sits at a bottom, $n=a_n$, so $E_iu=\sum_n[a_n-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}u_n=\sum_nF_i^{(n-1)}u_n=\tilde e_iu$ by [F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.5 Naturality. Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a homomorphism of weight-graded $A_i$-modules, so $\varphi$ commutes with $E_i$, $F_i$ and $K_i$ and preserves each $H_\mu$ and each weight space. Applying $\varphi$ to the admissible decomposition of $u$ gives the admissible decomposition of $\varphi(u)$ by uniqueness [F2], because $\varphi$ commutes with divided powers; hence $\varphi\tilde e_iu=\tilde e_i\varphi(u)$, $\varphi\tilde f_iu=\tilde f_i\varphi(u)$, and the same holds for the projections. [step 1.1, F2]

3.1 Interior comparison. In $L_i(2)$ take the highest vector $v=v_0$ and $u=F_iv=[1]_iv_1$; by [F3] $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$, whereas $u$ is the position-$1$ vector of the string of $v$ of length $2$, so $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$. Since $[2]_i=q_i+q_i^{-1}$ and $q_i$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $[2]_i\neq1$, so $\tilde f_i$ differs from $F_i$ at this interior position. [F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Definition

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_n)\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$, an index $i$, and for every $u\in M_\lambda$ its unique admissible decomposition $u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$.

[F1] $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$ with $K_h$ acting on $M_\mu$ by $q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$, $E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i}$, $F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}$, and $E_i,F_i$ locally nilpotent; a nonzero element of $H_\mu$ has $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and $F_i^{(n)}$ is injective on $H_\mu$ for $0\le n\le\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$ and zero for $n>\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$, with $h_i$ the simple coroot of the datum ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]], [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

[F2] The decomposition of [F1] is unique and $M_\lambda$ is the internal direct sum of the nonzero spaces $F_i^{(n)}H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$; in particular the coefficient $u_n$ and the position of each string are well defined ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

[F3] Divided powers satisfy $F_iF_i^{(n)}=[n+1]_iF_i^{(n+1)}$ and $E_iF_i^{(n)}w=[a-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}w$ for $w\in H_\mu$ with $a=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$; the module $L_i(2)$ of dimension $3$ has a highest vector $v$ with $F_iv=[1]_iv_1$, $F_iv_1=[2]_iv_2$, $F_iv_2=0$, and $[2]_i=q_i+q_i^{-1}\neq1$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]], parts (ii)-(iii), [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct. All operators are read off the unique string decomposition string by string.

1.1 Linearity and weights. On a string position $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ with $u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}$ put $\tilde e_i(F_i^{(n)}u_n):=F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ for $n\ge1$ and $0$ for $n=0$, and $\tilde f_i(F_i^{(n)}u_n):=F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$. By [F2] every $u$ is a unique sum of such positions inside its decomposition, so these prescriptions define linear maps on $M$; the shifted vectors lie in $M_{\lambda+\alpha_i}$ and $M_{\lambda-\alpha_i}$ respectively, since $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n\in M_{\lambda+\alpha_i}$ and $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n\in M_{\lambda-\alpha_i}$ by [F1]. [F1, F2]

2.1 The top projection. Writing $p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0$ gives a well-defined linear idempotent by [F2]. For $u=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}u_n$ one has $\tilde f_i\tilde e_iu=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n)}u_n$ by step 1.1, hence $u-\tilde f_i\tilde e_iu=u_0=p_{\mathrm{top}}u$; equivalently $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}}$, and on each position with $n\ge1$ the composition $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i$ is the identity. [step 1.1, F2]

2.2 The bottom projection. If $n\ge\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$, then $n$ equals that length by [F1], and $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n=0$ because $F_i^{(n)}$ is zero beyond the string length; thus $\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n<\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$, which is the admissible decomposition of $\tilde f_iu$ (its $m$-th top coefficient is $u_{m-1}$ for $m\ge1$). Applying step 1.1 to this decomposition, $\tilde e_i\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n<\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n$, so $u-\tilde e_i\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n=p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u$; in particular on each position that is not a bottom the composition $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i$ is the identity. [F1, step 1.1, F2]

2.3 Kernels. For $u=\sum_nF_i^{(n)}u_n$, step 1.1 gives $\tilde e_iu=0$ exactly when $u_n=0$ for all $n\ge1$, that is $u=u_0\in H_\lambda$. On the other hand [F3] gives $E_iu=\sum_{n\ge1}[a_n-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ with $a_n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$; here $a_n-n+1\ge1$ for $n\le a_n$ by admissibility and the term vanishes for $n>a_n$, so $E_iu=0$ exactly when $u_n=0$ for all $n\ge1$ as well; hence $\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i$. Likewise $\tilde f_iu=\sum_{n<a_n}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n=0$ exactly when $u_n=0$ for all $n<a_n$, and $F_iu=\sum_{n<a_n}[n+1]_iF_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ vanishes exactly then because $[n+1]_i\neq0$; hence $\ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i$. [F1, F3, step 1.1]

2.4 Agreement on the kernels. If $u\in\ker E_i$ then $u=u_0$ by [F2], so $\tilde f_iu=F_iu_0=F_iu$; if $u\in\ker F_i$ then every nonzero coefficient $u_n$ sits at a bottom, $n=a_n$, so $E_iu=\sum_n[a_n-n+1]_iF_i^{(n-1)}u_n=\sum_nF_i^{(n-1)}u_n=\tilde e_iu$ by [F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.5 Naturality. Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be a homomorphism of weight-graded $A_i$-modules, so $\varphi$ commutes with $E_i$, $F_i$ and $K_i$ and preserves each $H_\mu$ and each weight space. Applying $\varphi$ to the admissible decomposition of $u$ gives the admissible decomposition of $\varphi(u)$ by uniqueness [F2], because $\varphi$ commutes with divided powers; hence $\varphi\tilde e_iu=\tilde e_i\varphi(u)$, $\varphi\tilde f_iu=\tilde f_i\varphi(u)$, and the same holds for the projections. [step 1.1, F2]

3.1 Interior comparison. In $L_i(2)$ take the highest vector $v=v_0$ and $u=F_iv=[1]_iv_1$; by [F3] $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$, whereas $u$ is the position-$1$ vector of the string of $v$ of length $2$, so $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$. Since $[2]_i=q_i+q_i^{-1}$ and $q_i$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $[2]_i\neq1$, so $\tilde f_i$ differs from $F_i$ at this interior position. [F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Definition

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed $i\in I$, the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and
its generated subalgebras, the root grading and the height
$\operatorname{ht}:Q_+\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), and the finite words
$w=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_m}$ ($m\ge0$, the empty word for $m=0$) in the negative
generators.

[F1] The multiplication
$U_q^-\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^0\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^+\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$
is a vector-space isomorphism, and the $K_h$ ($h\in P^{\vee}$) are linearly
independent; every element of $U_q^-$ is a finite $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear
combination of words in the $F_j$; the root grading
$U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ has
$U_q^-[-\nu]\,U_q^0\subseteq U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\nu]$ and the images of the
subspaces $U_q^-[-\nu]\otimes U_q^0\otimes\mathbb Q(q)$ for distinct $\nu$ are
linearly independent ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

[F2] For homogeneous $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of degree $\beta$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,
$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x$, hence $K_hx=q^{\beta(h)}xK_h$ and
$K_h^{-1}x=q^{-\beta(h)}xK_h^{-1}$; in particular
$K_iF_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_jK_i$ and $K_i^{-1}F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_jK_i^{-1}$
( [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]] for $\operatorname{wt}(F_j)=-\alpha_j$).

[F3] $E_iF_j-F_jE_i=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F4] $\psi$ is an involutive semilinear algebra automorphism of
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$,
$\psi(K_h)=K_{-h}$; it preserves $U_q^-$ ([[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]]).

[F5] The height is additive: $\operatorname{ht}(\nu-\alpha_i)=\operatorname{ht}(\nu)-1$
for $\nu-\alpha_i\in Q_+$; if $\nu-k\alpha_i\in Q_+$ then
$\operatorname{ht}(\nu-k\alpha_i)=\operatorname{ht}(\nu)-k\ge0$, so there is no
word of that degree once $k>\operatorname{ht}(\nu)$; and the degrees of the
direct sum $\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ are pairwise distinct
([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

[F6] $q_i=q^{d_i}$ with $d_i>0$, so $q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(q)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** Construct $Q_w,R_w$ on words by moving $E_i$ to the right,
prove the defining identity on words by induction, and obtain existence and
uniqueness for all elements from [F1] and the linear independence of the toral
coefficients.

1.1 For each word $w=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_m}$ define $Q_w,R_w\in U_q^-$ by recursion on $m$: for the empty word $Q_1:=R_1:=0$, and for $m\ge1$, with $w'=F_{j_2}\cdots F_{j_m}$, set
$Q_w:=q_i^{a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}Q_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w'$ and
$R_w:=q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}R_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w'$.
Each is a finite $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear combination of words, hence an element of $U_q^-$; and $\deg Q_w=\deg R_w=-\nu$ whenever $\deg w=-\nu$, because $Q_{w'},R_{w'}$ have degree $\deg w'$ inductively and $F_{j_1}U_q^-[-\nu']\subseteq U_q^-[ -(\nu'+\alpha_{j_1})]$. [given, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 For every word $w$ one has $E_iw-wE_i=(K_iQ_w-K_i^{-1}R_w)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. For $m=0$ both sides vanish. For $m\ge1$, write $w=F_{j_1}w'$. Multiplying the inductive identity for $w'$ by $F_{j_1}$ on the left gives $E_iw=F_{j_1}w'E_i+F_{j_1}K_iQ_{w'}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})-F_{j_1}K_i^{-1}R_{w'}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, and [F3] gives $E_iF_{j_1}-F_{j_1}E_i=\delta_{ij_1}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Adding, and using [F2] in the form $F_{j_1}K_i=q_i^{a_{ij_1}}K_iF_{j_1}$, $F_{j_1}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}K_i^{-1}F_{j_1}$, yields $E_iw-wE_i=\bigl(K_i(q_i^{a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}Q_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w')-K_i^{-1}(q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}R_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w')\bigr)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=(K_iQ_w-K_i^{-1}R_w)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, which is the claim. [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 Existence follows for every $P\in U_q^-$: by [F1] write $P=\sum_wc_ww$ as a finite linear combination of words, and set $Q:=\sum_wc_wQ_w$, $R:=\sum_wc_wR_w$. Summing the identities of step 2.1 with coefficients $c_w$ gives $E_iP-PE_i=(K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 For uniqueness suppose $K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R=0$ with $Q,R\in U_q^-$. Decompose $Q=\sum_{\nu}Q_{\nu}$, $R=\sum_{\nu}R_{\nu}$ into the finitely many homogeneous components with $Q_{\nu},R_{\nu}\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). By [F2], $K_iQ_{\nu}-K_i^{-1}R_{\nu}=q_i^{-\nu(h_i)}Q_{\nu}K_i^2-q_i^{\nu(h_i)}R_{\nu}$ after multiplying on the right by $K_i$; the terms for distinct $\nu$ lie in distinct degrees $-\nu$ of the direct sum [F1], so for every $\nu$ the identity $q_i^{-\nu(h_i)}Q_{\nu}\otimes K_i^2=q_i^{\nu(h_i)}R_{\nu}\otimes1$ holds in $U_q^-[-\nu]\otimes U_q^0$ under the injective multiplication map. Applying $\mathrm{id}\otimes\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the linear functional on $U_q^0$ with $\lambda(K_{2d_ih_i})=1$ and $\lambda(K_h)=0$ for $h\ne2d_ih_i$ (existence and well-definedness by the linear independence in [F1]), gives $Q_{\nu}=0$; then $R_{\nu}=0$. Hence $Q=R=0$, and two pairs $(Q,R)$, $(Q',R')$ giving the same commutator have $Q=Q'$ and $R=R'$. [step 3.1, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

5.1 Consequently $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are well defined on all of $U_q^-$; they are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear because the defining identity is linear in $P$: if $P=c_1P_1+c_2P_2$, the pairs $(c_1Q(P_1)+c_2Q(P_2),\,c_1R(P_1)+c_2R(P_2))$ satisfy the defining identity for $P$, so by uniqueness each map is linear. The recursion gives $Q_1=R_1=0$, hence $e_i'(1)=e_i''(1)=0$; and for the one-letter word $w=F_j$ the recursion gives $Q_{F_j}=R_{F_j}=\delta_{ij}$, hence $e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F4, algebra]

5.2 For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$ decompose $E_i(xy)-(xy)E_i=(E_ix-xE_i)y+x(E_iy-yE_i)$ and substitute the defining identities for $x$ and $y$: the right side equals $\bigl(K_ie_i''(x)y-K_i^{-1}e_i'(x)y+xK_ie_i''(y)-xK_i^{-1}e_i'(y)\bigr)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. By [F2] with $\operatorname{wt}(x)$ in place of $\beta$, $xK_i=K_iq_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x$ and $xK_i^{-1}=K_i^{-1}q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x$. Collecting the $K_i$- and $K_i^{-1}$-coefficients and using the uniqueness of step 4.1 yields the two twisted Leibniz rules of (b). [step 4.1, F2, algebra]

6.1 For the grading and nilpotence, let $w$ be a word of degree $-\nu$, $\nu\in Q_+$. If $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$ then $Q_w=R_w=0$: indeed in the recursion $Q_{w}=q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}Q_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w'$ the inductive hypothesis is $Q_{w'}=R_{w'}=0$ because $\deg w'=\deg w-\alpha_{j_1}$ satisfies $(\nu-\alpha_i)-\alpha_{j_1}\notin Q_+$, while the term $\delta_{ij_1}w'$ is zero unless $j_1=i$, and $j_1=i$ would give $\nu-\alpha_i=\deg w'\in Q_+$, a contradiction. If $\nu-\alpha_i\in Q_+$, the recursion exhibits $Q_w,R_w$ as elements of $U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)]$. By linearity the same holds for every element of $U_q^-[-\nu]$. Hence $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ shift the degree by $+\alpha_i$, lower the height by one by [F5], and $(e_i')^{k}$ and $(e_i'')^{k}$ annihilate $U_q^-[-\nu]$ once $k>\operatorname{ht}(\nu)$ (and annihilate all of $U_q^-$ on each finite-dimensional homogeneous piece). [step 1.1, step 5.1, F5, algebra]

6.2 The commutation relations of (c) are the case $x=F_j$ of the Leibniz rules: $\operatorname{wt}(F_j)=-\alpha_j$, so $q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_j),h_i\rangle}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}$ and $q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_j),h_i\rangle}=q_i^{a_{ij}}$, while $e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ by step 5.1. Reading the resulting identities $e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y$ and $e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y$ as operator identities gives (c). [step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra]

7.1 For the bar relation, apply the semilinear algebra automorphism $\psi$ of [F4] to the defining identity of $P$: since $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(K_i)=K_i^{-1}$ and $\psi(q_i-q_i^{-1})=-(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, one gets $E_i\psi(P)-\psi(P)E_i=(K_i\psi(e_i'(P))-K_i^{-1}\psi(e_i''(P)))/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Comparing with the defining identity for $\psi(P)$, namely $E_i\psi(P)-\psi(P)E_i=(K_ie_i''(\psi(P))-K_i^{-1}e_i'(\psi(P)))/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, uniqueness (step 4.1) gives $e_i''(\psi(P))=\psi(e_i'(P))$ and $e_i'(\psi(P))=\psi(e_i''(P))$. Applying the second identity to $\psi(P)$ in place of $P$ and using $\psi^2=\mathrm{id}$ gives $e_i''(P)=\psi(e_i'(\psi(P)))$, that is, $e_i''=\psi e_i'\psi$. This proves (a)–(e) and completes the definition. [step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 5.2, step 6.2, F4, algebra] ∎

The last display also explains the orientation: replacing $\psi$ by the identity would exchange $e_i'$ and $e_i''$, and it is the commutator display (not an arbitrary convention) that selects the $K_i^{-1}$-coefficient as $e_i'$.

## Definition

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed $i\in I$, the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and
its generated subalgebras, the root grading and the height
$\operatorname{ht}:Q_+\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), and the finite words
$w=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_m}$ ($m\ge0$, the empty word for $m=0$) in the negative
generators.

[F1] The multiplication
$U_q^-\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^0\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^+\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$
is a vector-space isomorphism, and the $K_h$ ($h\in P^{\vee}$) are linearly
independent; every element of $U_q^-$ is a finite $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear
combination of words in the $F_j$; the root grading
$U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ has
$U_q^-[-\nu]\,U_q^0\subseteq U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\nu]$ and the images of the
subspaces $U_q^-[-\nu]\otimes U_q^0\otimes\mathbb Q(q)$ for distinct $\nu$ are
linearly independent ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

[F2] For homogeneous $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of degree $\beta$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,
$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x$, hence $K_hx=q^{\beta(h)}xK_h$ and
$K_h^{-1}x=q^{-\beta(h)}xK_h^{-1}$; in particular
$K_iF_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_jK_i$ and $K_i^{-1}F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_jK_i^{-1}$
( [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]] for $\operatorname{wt}(F_j)=-\alpha_j$).

[F3] $E_iF_j-F_jE_i=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F4] $\psi$ is an involutive semilinear algebra automorphism of
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$,
$\psi(K_h)=K_{-h}$; it preserves $U_q^-$ ([[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]]).

[F5] The height is additive: $\operatorname{ht}(\nu-\alpha_i)=\operatorname{ht}(\nu)-1$
for $\nu-\alpha_i\in Q_+$; if $\nu-k\alpha_i\in Q_+$ then
$\operatorname{ht}(\nu-k\alpha_i)=\operatorname{ht}(\nu)-k\ge0$, so there is no
word of that degree once $k>\operatorname{ht}(\nu)$; and the degrees of the
direct sum $\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ are pairwise distinct
([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

[F6] $q_i=q^{d_i}$ with $d_i>0$, so $q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(q)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** Construct $Q_w,R_w$ on words by moving $E_i$ to the right,
prove the defining identity on words by induction, and obtain existence and
uniqueness for all elements from [F1] and the linear independence of the toral
coefficients.

1.1 For each word $w=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_m}$ define $Q_w,R_w\in U_q^-$ by recursion on $m$: for the empty word $Q_1:=R_1:=0$, and for $m\ge1$, with $w'=F_{j_2}\cdots F_{j_m}$, set
$Q_w:=q_i^{a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}Q_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w'$ and
$R_w:=q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}R_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w'$.
Each is a finite $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear combination of words. If $w$ has degree $-\nu$, every nonzero term of $Q_w,R_w$ has degree $-\nu+\alpha_i$: inductively a nonzero $Q_{w'},R_{w'}$ has degree $\deg w'+\alpha_i$, multiplication by $F_{j_1}$ gives $\deg w+\alpha_i$, and the term $\delta_{ij_1}w'$ has that degree when $j_1=i$. [given, F1, F2, construct]

2.1 For every word $w$ one has $E_iw-wE_i=(K_iQ_w-K_i^{-1}R_w)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. For $m=0$ both sides vanish. For $m\ge1$, write $w=F_{j_1}w'$. Multiplying the inductive identity for $w'$ by $F_{j_1}$ on the left gives $E_iw=F_{j_1}w'E_i+F_{j_1}K_iQ_{w'}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})-F_{j_1}K_i^{-1}R_{w'}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, and [F3] gives $E_iF_{j_1}-F_{j_1}E_i=\delta_{ij_1}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Adding, and using [F2] in the form $F_{j_1}K_i=q_i^{a_{ij_1}}K_iF_{j_1}$, $F_{j_1}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}K_i^{-1}F_{j_1}$, yields $E_iw-wE_i=\bigl(K_i(q_i^{a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}Q_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w')-K_i^{-1}(q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}R_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w')\bigr)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=(K_iQ_w-K_i^{-1}R_w)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, which is the claim. [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 Existence follows for every $P\in U_q^-$: by [F1] write $P=\sum_wc_ww$ as a finite linear combination of words, and set $Q:=\sum_wc_wQ_w$, $R:=\sum_wc_wR_w$. Summing the identities of step 2.1 with coefficients $c_w$ gives $E_iP-PE_i=(K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 For uniqueness suppose $K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R=0$ with $Q,R\in U_q^-$. Decompose $Q=\sum_{\nu}Q_{\nu}$, $R=\sum_{\nu}R_{\nu}$ into the finitely many homogeneous components with $Q_{\nu},R_{\nu}\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). By [F2], $K_iQ_{\nu}-K_i^{-1}R_{\nu}=q_i^{-\nu(h_i)}Q_{\nu}K_i^2-q_i^{\nu(h_i)}R_{\nu}$ after multiplying on the right by $K_i$; the terms for distinct $\nu$ lie in distinct degrees $-\nu$ of the direct sum [F1], so for every $\nu$ the identity $q_i^{-\nu(h_i)}Q_{\nu}\otimes K_i^2=q_i^{\nu(h_i)}R_{\nu}\otimes1$ holds in $U_q^-[-\nu]\otimes U_q^0$ under the injective multiplication map. Applying $\mathrm{id}\otimes\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the linear functional on $U_q^0$ with $\lambda(K_{2d_ih_i})=1$ and $\lambda(K_h)=0$ for $h\ne2d_ih_i$ (existence and well-definedness by the linear independence in [F1]), gives $Q_{\nu}=0$; then $R_{\nu}=0$. Hence $Q=R=0$, and two pairs $(Q,R)$, $(Q',R')$ giving the same commutator have $Q=Q'$ and $R=R'$. [step 3.1, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

5.1 Consequently $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are well defined on all of $U_q^-$; they are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear because the defining identity is linear in $P$: if $P=c_1P_1+c_2P_2$, the pairs $(c_1Q(P_1)+c_2Q(P_2),\,c_1R(P_1)+c_2R(P_2))$ satisfy the defining identity for $P$, so by uniqueness each map is linear. The recursion gives $Q_1=R_1=0$, hence $e_i'(1)=e_i''(1)=0$; and for the one-letter word $w=F_j$ the recursion gives $Q_{F_j}=R_{F_j}=\delta_{ij}$, hence $e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F4, algebra]

5.2 For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$ decompose $E_i(xy)-(xy)E_i=(E_ix-xE_i)y+x(E_iy-yE_i)$ and substitute the defining identities for $x$ and $y$: the right side equals $\bigl(K_ie_i''(x)y-K_i^{-1}e_i'(x)y+xK_ie_i''(y)-xK_i^{-1}e_i'(y)\bigr)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. By [F2] with $\operatorname{wt}(x)$ in place of $\beta$, $xK_i=K_iq_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x$ and $xK_i^{-1}=K_i^{-1}q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x$. Collecting the $K_i$- and $K_i^{-1}$-coefficients and using the uniqueness of step 4.1 yields the two twisted Leibniz rules of (b). [step 4.1, F2, algebra]

6.1 Grading and nilpotence. The degree computation of step 1.1 shows that for a word $w$ of degree $-\nu$, every nonzero term of $Q_w,R_w$ has degree $-\nu+\alpha_i$. These are negative words, so both coefficients vanish if $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$; otherwise they belong to $U_q^-[-(\nu-\alpha_i)]$. By linearity the same holds on every homogeneous component. Thus $e_i',e_i''$ raise actual degree by $\alpha_i$ and lower positive height by one, and their $k$-th powers vanish on degree $-\nu$ for $k>\operatorname{ht}(\nu)$. Every vector has finite homogeneous support, so both maps are locally nilpotent. [step 1.1, step 5.1, F5, algebra]

6.2 The commutation relations of (c) are the case $x=F_j$ of the Leibniz rules: $\operatorname{wt}(F_j)=-\alpha_j$, so $q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_j),h_i\rangle}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}$ and $q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_j),h_i\rangle}=q_i^{a_{ij}}$, while $e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ by step 5.1. Reading the resulting identities $e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y$ and $e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y$ as operator identities gives (c). [step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra]

7.1 For the bar relation, apply the semilinear algebra automorphism $\psi$ of [F4] to the defining identity of $P$: since $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(K_i)=K_i^{-1}$ and $\psi(q_i-q_i^{-1})=-(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, one gets $E_i\psi(P)-\psi(P)E_i=(K_i\psi(e_i'(P))-K_i^{-1}\psi(e_i''(P)))/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Comparing with the defining identity for $\psi(P)$, namely $E_i\psi(P)-\psi(P)E_i=(K_ie_i''(\psi(P))-K_i^{-1}e_i'(\psi(P)))/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, uniqueness (step 4.1) gives $e_i''(\psi(P))=\psi(e_i'(P))$ and $e_i'(\psi(P))=\psi(e_i''(P))$. Applying the second identity to $\psi(P)$ in place of $P$ and using $\psi^2=\mathrm{id}$ gives $e_i''(P)=\psi(e_i'(\psi(P)))$, that is, $e_i''=\psi e_i'\psi$. This proves (a)–(e) and completes the definition. [step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 5.2, step 6.2, F4, algebra] ∎

The last display also explains the orientation: replacing $\psi$ by the identity would exchange $e_i'$ and $e_i''$, and it is the commutator display (not an arbitrary convention) that selects the $K_i^{-1}$-coefficient as $e_i'$.

## Statement

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then
$P_i$ is a well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear map with $e_i'P_i=0$ that fixes
$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

(iii) Every $x\in U_A^-$ has a unique finite expansion
$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators
$\tilde e_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}x_n$ and
$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$
preserve $U_A^-$.

## Statement

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then

$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators

$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$

For the projection claim, apply step 4.1 to the expansion of an arbitrary $y$: $F_iy=\sum_{n\ge1}[n]_iF_i^{(n)}y_{n-1}$ decomposes with all string coefficients in $\ker e_i'$ and zero $n=0$ coefficient, so $P_i(F_iy)=0$ by the formula; hence $U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ with $P_i$ the projection along $F_iU_q^-$, and $x_0=P_ix\in U_A^-$ whenever $x\in U_A^-$. Finally the string operators of (iii) are well defined by the uniqueness of the expansion, and they preserve $U_A^-$ because they only shift the divided-power labels $n\mapsto n\pm1$ of the integral coefficients $x_n\in U_A^-$. No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ was used anywhere. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $\lambda\in P$, let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with its canonical
$P$-label grading and highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), and let
$\sigma$ be the linear contravariant anti-involution of
[[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]
($\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$,
$\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$).

(i) **Existence and uniqueness.** Define the $\lambda$-weight functional
$\eta\colon U_q(\mathfrak g)\to\mathbb Q(q)$ by $\eta(y):=$ the coefficient of
$v_\lambda$ in $yv_\lambda$ (so $\eta(y)$ is unchanged by adding an element of
the Verma ideal $J(\lambda)$, and $\eta(1)=1$). Then
$$B\bigl(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda\bigr):=\eta\bigl(\sigma(a)b\bigr)\qquad(a,b\in U_q^-)$$
is a well-defined bilinear form on $M(\lambda)$; it is homogeneous, normalized
($B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$) and $\sigma$-contravariant,
$B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$. It is the unique such form on $M(\lambda)$, in the
sense of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

(ii) **Radical and descent.** The radical
$\operatorname{rad}B=\{u:B(u,M(\lambda))=0\}$ equals the sum $N(\lambda)$ of all
proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$; consequently $B$ descends to a
nondegenerate normalized $\sigma$-contravariant form on the simple highest
weight quotient $L(\lambda)=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$.

(iii) **Rank-one norms and dominant singular vectors.** If
$m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ (that is, $\lambda$ dominant), then for
every $r\ge0$
$$B\bigl(F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda\bigr)=q_i^{\,r(m_i-r)}\binom{m_i}{r}_i,$$
with the Gaussian binomial interpreted as $0$ for $r>m_i$; in particular each
$F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$ lies in the radical, so $B$ factors through the Serre
quotient $M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$. (The same
computation proves the norm formula for every $\lambda$ and all $r$ for which
the right-hand side is read with $m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$.)

(iv) **Ordinary simplicity.** Let $V$ be an integrable cyclic graded quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ with support in $\lambda-Q_+$ on which the descended form is
nondegenerate. Then $V$ is simple as an ordinary module (not only as a graded
module).

(v) **Integrality of the lattice values.** If $\lambda$ is integral and
$V_A:=U_Av_\lambda=U_A^-v_\lambda\subseteq L(\lambda)$ is the highest lattice of
the Lusztig form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), then
$B(V_A,V_A)\subseteq A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. No perfectness of $B$ over $A$ is
asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\lambda\in P$, the Verma module $M(\lambda)=U_q^-v_\lambda$ with
label grading, the anti-involution $\sigma$, and the functional $\eta(y)=$ the
coefficient of $v_\lambda$ in $yv_\lambda$.

[F1] $M(\lambda)=U_qv_\lambda$, $M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\nu}=U_q^-[-\nu]v_\lambda$,
$M(\lambda)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$; the map $U_q^-\to M(\lambda)$,
$a\mapsto av_\lambda$, is a linear isomorphism; the Verma ideal is
$J(\lambda)=U_q(\mathfrak g)\langle E_i,\ K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\rangle$,
and $yv_\lambda=0$ if and only if $y\in J(\lambda)$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).

[F2] $\sigma$ is an involutive $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear anti-automorphism with
$\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$,
$\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$; it preserves the root grading up to sign
($\sigma$ multiplies root degrees by $-1$)
([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]],
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]]).

[F3] $\eta$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and factors through $J(\lambda)$; it
satisfies $\eta(K_hy)=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\eta(y)$ for all $y$, and
$\eta(F_i\cdot U_q(\mathfrak g))=0$: indeed $F_iyv_\lambda$ has label
$\mu-\alpha_i$ when $yv_\lambda$ has label $\mu\le\lambda$, which can equal
$\lambda$ only if some weight of $M(\lambda)$ equals $\lambda+\alpha_i$, and all
weights of $M(\lambda)$ lie in $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).

[F4] Triangular decomposition: $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is the direct sum over
$\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+$ of the subspaces $U_q^-[-\gamma]U_q^0U_q^+[\alpha]$, and
$U_q(\mathfrak g)=U_q^-U_q^0U_q^+$ as a vector space; for $y\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$
the image $yv_\lambda$ determines and is determined by the sum of the
$U_q^-[-\gamma]$-components of its normal form
([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F5] Rank-one reordering: for every $r\ge1$,
$E_iF_i^{(r)}=F_i^{(r)}E_i+F_i^{(r-1)}T_{i,1-r,1}$ and
$T_{i,1-r,1}v_\lambda=[m_i-r+1]_iv_\lambda$ with $m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$,
while $K_iF_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda=q_i^{m_i-2(r-1)}F_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda$
([[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] (iii),
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

[F6] Divided-power multiplication $F_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF_i^{(a+b)}$
and $\binom{m}{r}_i=0$ for $r>m$, with all Gaussian coefficients integer
Laurent polynomials in $q_i$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]],
[[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** build the form from the $\lambda$-weight functional, verify
contravariance on the three families of generators using the weight bound and
the Verma ideal, obtain symmetry from the uniqueness theorem for contravariant
forms, identify the radical with the sum of proper graded submodules by a
pairing argument, and compute the rank-one norms by the divided-power
recursion.

1.1 The functional $\eta$ and the formula. Since $a\mapsto av_\lambda$ is a linear isomorphism $U_q^-\to M(\lambda)$ by [F1], the assignment $B(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda):=\eta(\sigma(a)b)$ is a well-defined bilinear form. It is homogeneous: if $a\in U_q^-[-\nu]$, $b\in U_q^-[-\mu]$ then $\sigma(a)b$ has root degree $\nu-\mu$, and $\eta$ vanishes on elements of nonzero root degree (the coefficient of the degree-zero vector $v_\lambda$ in $yv_\lambda$ vanishes when $y$ has nonzero degree, by the grading of $M(\lambda)$); hence $B$ vanishes unless $\nu=\mu$. It is normalized: $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=\eta(\sigma(1)1)=\eta(1)=1$. [given, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 Contravariance on generators. (a) For $x=F_j$: $B(F_jav_\lambda,bv_\lambda)=\eta(\sigma(a)\sigma(F_j)b)=B(av_\lambda,\sigma(F_j)bv_\lambda)$ is a tautology of associativity. (b) For $x=K_h$: $K_hav_\lambda=q^{\langle\lambda-\nu,h\rangle}av_\lambda$ if $a\in U_q^-[-\nu]$, so $B(K_hav_\lambda,bv_\lambda)=q^{\langle\lambda-\nu,h\rangle}B(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda)$ while $B(av_\lambda,\sigma(K_h)bv_\lambda)=B(av_\lambda,K_hbv_\lambda)$ and $K_hbv_\lambda=q^{\langle\lambda-\mu,h\rangle}bv_\lambda$; both quantities vanish unless the labels match ($\nu=\mu$, forced by the homogeneity of $B$), in which case the two scalars agree. (c) For $x=E_i$: write $E_ia=aE_i+w$ with $w=(K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, $Q=e_i''(a)$, $R=e_i'(a)\in U_q^-$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), so $E_iav_\lambda=wv_\lambda$ and the coordinate of $E_iav_\lambda$ is the normal form $\mathrm{nf}(w)\in U_q^-$ of $w$. For every $b\in U_q^-$ one has $E_ia-\mathrm{nf}(w)\in J(\lambda)$, and $\sigma(J(\lambda))U_q^-\subseteq\ker\eta$: indeed $J(\lambda)=U_q(\mathfrak g)\langle E_i,K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\rangle$, so $\sigma(J(\lambda))=\langle\sigma(E_i),\sigma(K_h)-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\rangle U_q(\mathfrak g)$, and $\eta$ kills $\bigl(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\bigr)U_q(\mathfrak g)$ by $\eta(K_hy)=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\eta(y)$ of [F3], while it kills $\sigma(E_i)U_q(\mathfrak g)U_q^-=\sigma(E_i)U_q(\mathfrak g)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}U_q(\mathfrak g)$ by $\eta(F_iU_q(\mathfrak g))=0$ of [F3]. Hence $\eta(\sigma(\mathrm{nf}(w))b)=\eta(\sigma(w)b)$, and therefore $B(E_iav_\lambda,bv_\lambda)=\eta(\sigma(w)b)=\eta(\sigma(a)\sigma(E_i)b)=B(av_\lambda,\sigma(E_i)bv_\lambda)$. Since the set of $x$ for which $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ holds for all $u,v$ is a subalgebra of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ (if it holds for $x$ and $y$, then $B(xyu,v)=B(yu,\sigma(x)v)=B(u,\sigma(y)\sigma(x)v)=B(u,\sigma(xy)v)$) and contains the generators by (a)-(c), the form is $\sigma$-contravariant. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

3.1 Symmetry. Let $B^{t}(u,v):=B(v,u)$ be the transpose. Then $B^{t}(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ and $B^{t}$ is $\sigma$-contravariant: $B^{t}(xu,v)=B(v,xu)=B(\sigma(x)v,u)=B^{t}(u,\sigma(x)v)$, using step 2.1 and $\sigma^{2}=\mathrm{id}$. By the uniqueness part of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]] (a $\sigma$-contravariant bilinear form on a normalized highest weight module with value $1$ on the top vector is unique), $B^{t}=B$, i.e. $B$ is symmetric. [step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 The radical equals $N(\lambda)$. The radical of a contravariant form is a submodule ($B(xu,v)=0$ for $u\in\operatorname{rad}B$ and all $v$ implies $B(u,\sigma(x)v)=0$), it is homogeneous by step 1.1, and it is proper because $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$. Hence $\operatorname{rad}B$ is a proper graded submodule and $\operatorname{rad}B\subseteq N(\lambda)$. Conversely let $n\in N(\lambda)$ have label $\lambda-\nu$ and let $b\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ be arbitrary. By symmetry and contravariance, $B(n,bv_\lambda)=B(bv_\lambda,n)=B(v_\lambda,\sigma(b)n)$; now $\sigma(b)n\in U_q(\mathfrak g)N(\lambda)\subseteq N(\lambda)$ and $\sigma(b)n$ has label $\lambda$ because $b$ has label $\nu$ and $n$ has label $\lambda-\nu$, so $\sigma(b)n\in N(\lambda)_\lambda=N(\lambda)\cap M(\lambda)_\lambda=0$ because $N(\lambda)$ is proper graded and $M(\lambda)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ with $v_\lambda\notin N(\lambda)$. Hence $B(n,bv_\lambda)=0$; since the $bv_\lambda$ with $b\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ span $M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\nu}$ and $B(n,\cdot)$ vanishes on all other graded pieces by homogeneity, $n\in\operatorname{rad}B$. Thus $N(\lambda)\subseteq\operatorname{rad}B$ and the two agree. Consequently the induced form on $L(\lambda)=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$ is well defined, normalized, contravariant and nondegenerate (if $\bar u$ pairs to zero with all of $L(\lambda)$ then $u$ pairs to zero with all of $M(\lambda)$, so $u\in\operatorname{rad}B=N(\lambda)$, i.e. $\bar u=0$). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F1, algebra]

5.1 Rank-one norms. Write $N_r:=B(F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)$ and $m=m_i$. For $r\ge1$ use contravariance with $x=F_i$: since $F_iF_i^{(r-1)}=[r]_iF_i^{(r)}$ [F6], $N_r=[r]_i^{-1}B(F_iF_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)=[r]_i^{-1}B(F_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda,\sigma(F_i)F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)=[r]_i^{-1}q_i^{-1}B(F_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda,K_iE_iF_i^{(r)}v_\lambda)$. By [F5], $E_iF_i^{(r)}v_\lambda=F_i^{(r-1)}T_{i,1-r,1}v_\lambda=F_i^{(r-1)}[m-r+1]_iv_\lambda$, so $K_iE_iF_i^{(r)}v_\lambda=[m-r+1]_iq_i^{m-2(r-1)}F_i^{(r-1)}v_\lambda$ and $N_r=[r]_i^{-1}q_i^{m-2r+1}[m-r+1]_iN_{r-1}$. With $N_0=1$, induction gives $N_r=\prod_{k=1}^{r}q_i^{m-2k+1}\frac{[m-k+1]_i}{[k]_i}=q_i^{m-r(r+1)+r}\frac{[m]_i\cdots[m-r+1]_i}{[1]_i\cdots[r]_i}=q_i^{r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_i$, since $\sum_{k=1}^{r}(m-2k+1)=rm-r^2$; when $r>m$ the factor $[m-r+1]_i=0$ appears and the product vanishes, and $\binom{m}{r}_i=0$ by [F6]. For $r=m_i+1$ this gives $N_{m_i+1}=0$; moreover for any word $w$ of degree $-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$ one has $w=cF_i^{(m_i+1)}$ because $U_q^-[-(m_i+1)\alpha_i]$ is spanned by the single word $F_i^{m_i+1}$, so $B(F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda,wv_\lambda)=0$ for all $w$, i.e. $F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda\in\operatorname{rad}B=N(\lambda)$ by step 4.1. [step 2.1, step 4.1, F5, F6, algebra]

6.1 Ordinary simplicity. Let $V=M(\lambda)/Q$ be an integrable cyclic graded quotient with support in $\lambda-Q_+$ on which the descended form (still written $B$) is nondegenerate, and let $0\ne W\subseteq V$ be an ordinary (not necessarily graded) submodule. Choose $0\ne x\in W$ and write $x=\sum_jx_j$ with $x_j$ homogeneous of label $\mu_j\in\lambda-Q_+$; choose among the finitely many $\mu_j$ one that is maximal for the order $\mu\le\lambda$ (a finite set has a maximal element). Since $B$ is nondegenerate, there is $v\in V$ with $B(x,v)\ne0$; writing $v=\sum_kb_kv_\lambda$ with $b_k\in U_q^-$ homogeneous (possible because $V$ is generated by $v_\lambda$) and using homogeneity of $B$, some $b_k$ of label $\lambda-\mu_j$ satisfies $B(x_j,b_kv_\lambda)\ne0$. Then $y:=\sigma(b_k)x_j\in W$ has label $\lambda$ (as $\sigma$ multiplies root degrees by $-1$), so $y\in V_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)\bar v_\lambda$, and $y\ne0$ because $B(y,\bar v_\lambda)=B(x_j,b_kv_\lambda)\ne0$ by contravariance and symmetry. Hence $\bar v_\lambda\in W$, and since $V=U_q(\mathfrak g)\bar v_\lambda$, $W=V$: $V$ is ordinary-simple. [step 4.1, step 5.1, F1, F2, algebra]

7.1 Integrality. Let $\lambda$ be integral and $a,b\in U_A^-$. By the stability computation of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]] (applied to $\sigma$ in place of the two involutions named there: $\sigma(E_i^{(r)})=q_i^rF_i^{(r)}K_i^{-r}$ and $\sigma(F_i^{(r)})=q_i^{-r}K_i^rE_i^{(r)}$ lie in $U_A$, and $\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}$), one has $\sigma(a)b\in U_A$. Write $\sigma(a)b$ in the triangular spanning form $\sigma(a)b=\sum_tb_tu_tc_t$ with $b_t\in U_A^-$, $u_t\in U_A^0$, $c_t\in U_A^+$ ([[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] (iv)). Then $\sigma(a)bv_\lambda=\sum_t\epsilon_t\chi_\lambda(u_t)b_tv_\lambda$ with $\epsilon_t$ the augmentation of $c_t$, so $\eta(\sigma(a)b)=\sum_t\epsilon_t\chi_\lambda(u_t)\varepsilon(b_t)$ with $\varepsilon$ the augmentation of $U_A^-$: each of these three factors lies in $A$, because $\varepsilon(U_A^\pm)\subseteq A$, $\chi_\lambda(K_h)=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}\in A$ and $\chi_\lambda(T_{i,c,t})=\left[\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle+c\ \mathrm{choose}\ t\right]_i$, a Gaussian binomial with integer upper entry, which is an integer Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ by [F6] (the negative upper entry is handled by the finite product formula $[x]_i$ and the Gaussian quotient identities). Hence $B(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda)=\eta(\sigma(a)b)\in A$, which is (v). No perfectness of $B$ over $A$ and no $A$-valuedness of the negative-half Kashiwara form is claimed. This completes the construction and the proof. [step 1.1, step 4.1, F5, F6, algebra] ∎
