## Statement

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and generating residue sets of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], let $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ be the Kashiwara operators, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the tensor maps of [[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]. For $\alpha=\sum_in_i\alpha_i\in Q_+$ write $|\alpha|:=\sum_in_i$ and $Q_+(r):=\{\alpha\in Q_+:\ |\alpha|\le r\}$.

(i) For every integer $r\ge0$ the following interlocking statements are all true.

- A(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for all $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- B(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- C(r): for all $i$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$.
- D(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- E(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$.
- F(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$.
- G(r): $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal B(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal B(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda+\mu)\cup\{0\}$ for all $\lambda,\mu$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- H(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- I(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- J(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$, one has $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$.
- K(r): $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- L(r): $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- M(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P^+$ and $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, one has $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$.
- N(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\pi_\lambda$ induces a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- O(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, one has $\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)=\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)$.

(ii) Consequently $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ is a crystal basis of $V(\lambda)$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is a crystal lattice of $V(\lambda)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$, the operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ and the partial-inverse axiom, and $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu=\#\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ for all $\mu$. The lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ are free $A_0$-modules.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Dominant integral weights $\lambda,\mu$, the simple integrable highest weight modules and the lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty)$ generated by the lowering words, the tensor maps $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu},S_{\lambda,\mu}$ and the operators with their string decompositions.

[F1] $V(\lambda)$ is simple and universally integrable cyclic of highest weight $\lambda$, with finite-dimensional weight spaces and support $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]], [[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).

[F2] $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_\mu\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$, $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_\nu\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ are generated over $A_0$ by the lowering words, with the recursive spanning $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_i\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ for $\alpha\neq0$ and the same for $\mathcal L(\infty)$; each component is finitely generated, torsionfree and free over the DVR $A_0$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[cor-finitely-generated-torsion-free-modules-over-a-pid-are-free]]).

[F3] Module operators: $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}}$, $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$, $\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i$, $\ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i$, and the string of an $E_i$-highest vector of rank-one weight $a$ has the positions $0,\dots,a$; the negative-half operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$, $\tilde e_iu=0$ iff $u\in\ker e_i'$, and $\tilde e_i$ lowers the root height by one ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]], [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]).

[F4] The maps $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ are the unique module maps with the prescribed top images, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}=\mathrm{id}$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is an isometry onto the cyclic highest summand, they are adjoint for the product form, and $S_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the unique $U_q^-$-linear retraction with $S_{\lambda,\mu}\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(v_{\lambda+\mu})=v_\lambda$ ([[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]).

[F5] Rank-one tensor rule: for tensors of rank-one divided strings, modulo $q$ the operator $\tilde f_i$ acts on the first factor when $\varphi_i(\text{first})>\varepsilon_i(\text{second})$ and on the second factor otherwise, $\tilde e_i$ acts on the first factor when $\varphi_i(\text{first})\ge\varepsilon_i(\text{second})$ and on the second otherwise, with the partial-inverse property on the resulting chains; the chains partition the rectangle of divided positions ([[lem-rank-one-tensor-strings-have-the-crystal-limit-rule]]).

[F6] Finite-support regularization: there is an auxiliary regular Cartan datum with a finite coordinate summand containing the finitely many top labels used and all simple roots, with integral fundamental weights $\Lambda_i$, independent simple roots, the same $d_i$ and Cartan matrix, and $K_i=K_{d_iH_i}$; it identifies the graded support categories and all operations used below, so auxiliary fundamental or large weights act as labels inside the same category ([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]]).

[F7] Negative-half form: the bilinear form on $U_q^-$ is symmetric, nondegenerate and $A$-valued on the word lattice, with the exact $A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ denominator bound on the divided lattice, the form on $V(\lambda)$ restricted through $\pi_\lambda$ is the contravariant form of [F4], and the nondegeneracy and rank comparison inherit the axiom of choice declared in [[def-axiom-of-choice]] ([[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]).

[F8] Finite matrix algebra: over a commutative ring a square matrix whose determinant is a unit is invertible, and over a local ring a finitely generated module is zero when its reduction modulo the maximal ideal is zero, by Nakayama ([[lem-determinant-trick-for-nakayama]], [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

[F9] The axiom of choice may be used as declared; all other arguments below are finite and choice-free ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** induction. Prove the interlocking clauses A(r)-O(r) simultaneously by induction on $r=|\alpha|$, in the order of the JKK grand loop: field spanning and the base cases, then string-component extraction, the rank-one tensor computations, the large-weight microlocal congruences, the lattice projections and the pairing steps, closing each clause at height $r$ before the next.

**JKK clause map.** The stages below follow [JKK §7] in the owner-corrected order: string components (7.3)-(7.4), rank-one tensors (7.5), E (7.6), the last-color-change splitting (7.7), the tensor-lattice decomposition (7.8), the large-weight microlocal congruences (7.10)-(7.11), M and L (7.12)-(7.14), A and H (7.15)-(7.17), I, O and B (7.21)-(7.24), the module pairing (7.25), the large-weight normalization (7.26, corrected), the dual transfer and special F (7.27)-(7.28), J (7.29), C (7.30), D and K (7.31), N (7.34), and general F and G (7.33 and 7.36, with Lemmas 7.32 and 7.35).

1.1 Field spanning by lowering words. For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$ the module $V(\lambda)$ is generated over $U_q^-$ by $v_\lambda$, and the root decomposition gives $V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}F_iV(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$; by induction on the height, $V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_w\mathbb Q(q)wv_\lambda$ over the words $w$ of total degree $\alpha$, and the same holds for $U_q^-[-\alpha]=\sum_iF_iU_q^-[-\alpha+\alpha_i]$. Since the $\tilde f_i$-words span the same spaces as the $F_i$-words by [F3], the $\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is $V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the span of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is $U_q^-[-\alpha]$. [F1, F2, F3]

1.2 The base of the induction. [base] For $r=0$ and $r=1$ all clauses hold: the only $\alpha$ are $0$ and the simple roots; the string of $v_\lambda$ has positions $0,\dots,\lambda(h_i)$, so $\tilde e_iv_\lambda=0$, $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i^nv_\lambda=\tilde f_i^{n-1}v_\lambda$ for $n\ge1$, and the top position of the $\tilde e_i$-string is detected by the finiteness of the module string; the unit $\mathbf 1\in U_q^-$ is killed by $\tilde e_i$ and satisfies $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$; on the one-dimensional spaces $\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ and $\mathbb Q(q)\mathbf 1$ the residue sets are $\{v_\lambda\}$ and $\{\mathbf 1\}$; and the tensor clauses are checked on top positions, where $v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu$ is the highest vector by [F4]. [base, F2, F3, F4]

1.3 Induction hypothesis. [ih] Fix $r\ge1$ and assume all clauses A-O for all heights $<r$; the induction then proves them at height $r$ in the steps below. All statements are made in the auxiliary regular datum of [F6] with its fundamental and arbitrarily large dominant weights, and are transported back to the original labels at the end. [ih, F6, given]

2.1 String components. Let $u\in\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ with $|\alpha|<r$ and let $u=\sum_{n=0}^NF_i^{(n)}u_n$ be its admissible $i$-string decomposition with $u_n\in\ker E_i$. Then every $u_n$ lies in $\mathcal L(\lambda)$: by [F3], $\tilde e_i^NF_i^{(n)}u_n=0$ for $n<N$ and $\tilde e_i^NF_i^{(N)}u_N=\gamma u_N$ with $\gamma\neq0$; A$(r-1)$ makes $\tilde e_i^Nu\in\mathcal L(\lambda)$, so $u_N=\gamma^{-1}\tilde e_i^Nu\in\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and subtracting $F_i^{(N)}u_N$ iterates the argument. Consequently, if $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is the residue of a lowering word, then modulo $q$ exactly one nonzero string component of a lift survives, by the lower-height clauses B and C, and that survivor is the residue of a unique top word; this is the residue form of the same statement. [F2, F3, step 1.3]

2.2 The rank-one tensor computations. Let $b\otimes b'$ be a tensor of two rank-one divided strings whose factor heights are $<r$. By [F5] the tensor lattice is stable under $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on these inputs, the comparisons are strict for $\tilde f_i$ ($\varphi_i(\text{first})>\varepsilon_i(\text{second})$) and non-strict for $\tilde e_i$ ($\varphi_i(\text{first})\ge\varepsilon_i(\text{second})$), and where both factor heights are below $r$ the partial-inverse property holds for the tensor basis; this includes the endpoint cases, where one factor is at its top or bottom and the other is not, because the vanishing is decided by the comparison of the two string lengths. [F5, step 1.3]

2.3 E(r). For $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, the component $\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha}$ is spanned by the images $\tilde f_i$ of the components at height $\alpha-\alpha_i$ (for $\alpha\ne0$) and by $A_0v_{\lambda+\mu}$ for $\alpha=0$; the map $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ is a module map, hence commutes with the $\tilde f_i$, and the induction hypothesis at height $<r$ gives $\tilde f_i\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha+\alpha_i})\subseteq\tilde f_i(\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))$; the tensor lattice is stable under $\tilde f_i$, so $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$. [F2, F4, step 1.3]

2.4 Large-weight microlocal congruence. On the $n$-th string position the operator $q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$ has the rank-one coefficient $q_i^{a-2n+1}[a-n+1]_i$, whose inverse has nonnegative $q$-valuation at admissible positions; if $q_i^{-1}K_iE_iu\in q^NL$, extracting string components places all positive top components in $q^NL$. For $P=F_i^{(n)}Q$ with $e_i'Q=0$ the exact identity $q_i^{-1}K_iE_i(Qv_\lambda)=-(1-q_i^2)^{-1}q_i^{2\langle h_i,\lambda+\alpha_i+\mathrm{wt}Q\rangle}(e_i''Q)v_\lambda$ shows that the error terms have arbitrarily high valuation once every $\lambda(h_j)$ is large, uniformly on the finitely many words of a fixed degree; hence both $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ commute with $\pi_\lambda$ modulo $q$ for large weights. [F2, F3, F6, step 1.1]

3.1 Splitting at the last color change. Let $w=\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ be a lowering word of height $r$ whose last color change is at position $t$, so $i_t\neq i_{t+1}=\cdots=i_r$, and let $\lambda_0=\Lambda_{i_t}$, $\mu$ large with $\lambda=\lambda_0+\mu$. Applying the coproduct to $v_{\lambda_0}\otimes v_\mu$, the first occurrence of $i_t$ lowers the first factor, while the repeated tail lowers the second factor; explicitly $E_{i_t}$ kills the repeated different-color tail and $F_{i_t}$ sends it to $F_{i_t}v_{\lambda_0}\otimes\text{tail}+q_{i_t}v_{\lambda_0}\otimes F_{i_t}\text{tail}$, whose second term lies in $q$ times the tensor lattice. Both factor degrees of the resulting residue are strictly between $0$ and $r$, so step 2.2 controls it and the prefix inputs have both heights below $r$. [F4, F5, F6, step 2.2]

3.2 M(r) and L(r). For arbitrary $\lambda$ add a sufficiently large $\mu$, apply $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}$ and the large-weight congruence of step 2.4 to the tensor top, use E$(r-1)$ and the lower-height projection, and apply the retraction $S_{\lambda,\mu}$, whose $\tilde f_i$-compatibility modulo $q$ follows by checking its top-second and positive-second string positions; this gives M(r). Iterating M(r) along a finite word gives $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and equality of word residues; recursive spanning gives $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})+q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the finitely generated quotient vanishes by [F8], proving L(r). Moreover $\pi_\lambda$ induces a surjection of residue spaces at each height $\le r$. [F2, F4, F8, step 2.4]

4.1 Tensor-lattice decomposition. Let $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$. Then $(\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i(\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha+\alpha_i}+\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\otimes A_0v_\mu$ modulo $q$: apply all raising operators $\tilde e_i$ to a tensor residue; if every one kills the residue, its first factor must be the top $v_\lambda$ by the lower-height partial inverse of step 2.2, giving the boundary term; otherwise take the predecessor given by the partial-inverse rule at lower height, and the first-boundary terms are congruent, at each prefix, to the same word applied to $v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu$ by the top-second tensor rule, with only the previous degree involved. [F4, F5, step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 Nakayama upgrade at lower height. The decomposition of step 4.1, together with the finite generation of the components in [F2], upgrades the generated residue span of $\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$ to lattice equality at height $<r$ without assuming a basis at height $r$: a finitely generated $A_0$-module whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal is spanned by the residue classes of the given elements equals the module generated by those elements, by [F8]. [F2, F8, step 4.1]

5.2 A(r) and H(r). Choose a common pole bound $N$ for $\tilde e_i$ on the finite set of labels and components under consideration; at large weight the large-weight isomorphism and the previous-degree bounds give the same bound. A tensor component of total degree $\alpha$ has the same bound: interior factor degrees are lower and already integral, and boundary degrees are handled by extracting positive string components in $q^{-N}$ and applying the rank-one tensor rule. If $N>0$, a pure-color word is checked exactly by rank one; every other word splits at its last color change into an interior tensor residue plus $q$ times the bounded tensor lattice by steps 3.1 and 4.1, so raising improves the bound to $q^{-N+1}$. Applying $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ in raised degree uses F$(r-1)$, not F(r); comparing a word on $v_\tau\otimes v_\mu$ with its first-factor word times $v_\mu$, the projection $\Phi$ in raised degree uses E$(r-1)$ and extracting the second top improves the bound by one power. Transfer to $U_q^-$ by its large-weight lattice isomorphism and microlocal congruence. Hence $N$ decreases by one at each round, terminates at $0$, and A(r), H(r) hold. [F2, F4, step 2.2, step 4.1, step 2.4]

6.1 I(r), O(r) and B(r). For a nonpure negative-half word use the interior tensor splitting of step 3.1, apply the rank-one tensor raising rule and the lower-height clauses B and G, then transport through the large-weight projection of step 2.4; the pure-color case is rank one, giving I(r). For O(r), take a surviving word residue in $V(\lambda)$: tensoring with a large second top gives the residue $u\otimes v_\mu$; raising on a top-second tensor is congruent to $\tilde e_iu\otimes v_\mu$ by the rank-one rule, and comparing with the large-weight negative-half raising calculation, applying $\Phi$ and then $S$, gives O(r). Then I(r), O(r) and the residue-image statement of step 3.2 give B(r), with no same-height C or F premise. [F4, F5, step 3.1, step 2.4, step 3.2, step 5.2]

6.2 The module lattice pairing. String extraction is justified by A(r). Homogeneous top string components of different positions are orthogonal, because repeated contravariance reduces their pairing to a highest vector paired with a positive $F_i$-power, which is zero; at equal position $n$ with top rank-one weight $a$, the exact norm factor is $q_i^{n(a-n)}\binom{a}{n}_i\in1+qA_0$. For a positive-height pair, recursively write one input as $\tilde f_i$ of a lower-height input, extract both strings and apply these unit norm ratios; this gives $\langle\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal L(\lambda)\rangle\subseteq A_0$ and $\langle\tilde f_iu,v\rangle\equiv\langle u,\tilde e_iv\rangle\bmod q$. At $n=0$ or $a=0$ the endpoint terms are zero, so no finite-string identity is misused. [F3, F4, step 5.2, algebra]

7.1 The large-weight pairing normalization, corrected. If $Q$ has degree $-\nu$ and $P=F_iR$ with actual weight $-\nu+\alpha_i$, the exact commutator gives $\langle F_iRv,Qv\rangle=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}[\langle Rv,(e_i'Q)v\rangle-q_i^{2\langle h_i,\lambda-\nu+\alpha_i\rangle}\langle Rv,(e_i''Q)v\rangle]$; inducting on height with $\langle F_iR,Q\rangle=\langle R,e_i'Q\rangle$ in the half shows that, for $\nu=\sum_in_i\alpha_i$, the constant term is $C_\nu\langle P,Q\rangle$ with $C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-n_i}\in1+qA_0$, so $\langle Pv,Qv\rangle\equiv C_\nu\langle P,Q\rangle$ modulo any prescribed $q$-order once every $\lambda(h_i)$ is large. The other term at each stage carries a large positive power of $q_i$, and its remaining lower-degree pairing is a finite polynomial in the variables $q_j^{2\lambda(h_j)}$ with bounded coefficients, uniformly for the finitely many vectors of a component; Kashiwara's constant-term lemma in §4 has the consistent constant term, and the printed factor direction of the corresponding grand-loop clause is not used. [F2, F7, step 1.1, step 6.2]

8.1 Field-dual lattice transfer and special F(r). Choose an $A_0$-basis $P_k$ of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and let $Q_j$ be its field dual under the nondegenerate field form of [F7], $\langle P_k,Q_j\rangle=\delta_{kj}$; define $\mathcal L(\infty)^\vee_{-\nu}:=\sum_jA_0Q_j$; the $Q_j$ need not lie in $\mathcal L(\infty)$, and this is the only place where the inherited axiom of choice of [F7] is used. The corrected comparison of step 7.1 gives $\langle P_kv,Q_jv\rangle\equiv\delta_{kj}\bmod q$ because $C_\nu\equiv1$; the pairing matrix is therefore invertible over $A_0$ by [F8], the large-weight field/lattice isomorphism gives $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)^\vee)=\mathcal L(\lambda)^\vee$, and $(\mathcal L(\lambda)^\vee)^\vee=\mathcal L(\lambda)$. For $\mu$ large, decompose the tensor lattice as in step 4.1; the lowering-image part passes through $\Psi$ by F$(r-1)$. Pair the remainder $v_\lambda\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$ with every $u\in\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)^\vee$; writing $u=Pv_{\lambda+\mu}$ with $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)^\vee$, only the extreme toral term of $\Delta P$ can pair with a first top, and its scalar is $q^{\sum_in_id_i\lambda(h_i)}\in A_0$ while $Pv_\mu\in\mathcal L(\mu)^\vee$; adjointness therefore places $\Psi$ of that remainder in the double dual $\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$, proving special F(r) for large $\mu$ without assuming unimodularity. [F4, F7, F8, step 4.1, step 7.1]

9.1 J(r). For a nonpure lowering word use its fundamental/large-weight interior tensor residue of step 3.1, whose two factor heights are $<r$. If its raised negative-half residue is nonzero, large-weight raising compatibility and the lower clause G make the tensor raised residue nonzero, and the lower tensor partial inverse gives $b_{\mathrm{tensor}}=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib_{\mathrm{tensor}}$; applying $\Psi$ to this degree-$r$ congruence using special F(r) of step 8.1, and using the large-weight lattice isomorphism and operator congruences of step 2.4, gives $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$ in $U_q^-$. The pure-color word uses the exact infinite-string identity $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$. This uses no same-height self-duality, general F or N. [F3, F5, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 2.4, step 8.1]

10.1 C(r). For a surviving module edge, string extraction and the lower partial-inverse clauses give C(r) in one direction; for its converse, lift through the lower clauses L and O and apply J(r) of step 9.1. [step 2.1, step 3.2, step 6.1, step 9.1]

10.2 N(r). N(r) is the residue surjectivity of step 3.2 together with injectivity: if two surviving preimages have the same module image, raise by an index $i$ that does not kill that common image, use O(r) and the lower clause N$(r-1)$ to see that the raised negative-half residues agree, and apply J(r) to conclude that the two preimages were equal. [step 3.2, step 6.1, step 9.1]

11.1 D(r) and K(r). Take a finite linear relation among the residue classes of the lowering words at height $r$ and apply each $\tilde e_i$: below $r$ the raised residues form an independent basis, and the partial-inverse statement makes the surviving preimages under each $\tilde e_i$ distinct, so every positive-degree word residue has a nonzero raising edge — in $V(\lambda)$ it is a $\tilde f_i$-predecessor and the string-component argument gives the inverse, in $U_q^-$ the identity $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ on the lattice does. Hence every coefficient of the relation vanishes; recursive definitions give spanning, so D(r) and K(r) hold. [F2, F3, step 2.1, step 6.1, step 10.1]

12.1 General F(r) and G(r). Once D$(r)$ and K$(r)$ and the partial inverse are proved, a residue killed by all $\tilde e_i$ in positive height is zero, by independence of the raised predecessor residues. If a field vector has all raisings in the lattice, take its minimal $q$-pole $N$; if $N>0$, its normalized nonzero residue is killed by all raisings, a contradiction, so the vector lies in the lattice. Applying this to $\Psi$ of an arbitrary tensor lattice element, whose raisings lie in the lattice by tensor stability at height $r$ and F$(r-1)$, proves general F(r). For a tensor basis residue, if every raising vanishes then its $\Psi$-image vanishes by the same residue detection; otherwise the tensor partial inverse, the lower clause G and the commutation of $\Psi$ with the operators produce a basis word or zero, which is G(r). [F4, F5, step 11.1]

13.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.2, 2.3, 3.2, 5.2, 6.1 and 9.1-12.1 prove A(r)-O(r) for every $r$ by induction, so all clauses hold at all heights. Then $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is a free $A_0$-module by [F2] with $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\lambda)=V(\lambda)$ by step 1.1, stable under both operators by A(r); $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with the graded decomposition and operator stability by B, D and the definition, and the partial-inverse axiom is C(r); hence $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ is a crystal basis in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]. The rank equality $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu=\#\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ follows from the lattice splitting and D(r), and the negative-half statements give $\mathcal B(\infty)$ with the same properties, with the formal $\varphi_i$ of [[def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight]]. The transported labels are the original ones by [F6]. No global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness, tensor-crystal theorem or $A_0$-perfectness premise is used; the only choice used is the inherited one of step 8.1, as declared in [F9]. [F6, F7, F8, F9, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 12.1, discharge-induction] ∎

## Statement

For the highest-module and negative-half Kashiwara lattices, their respective normalized polarizations take values in $A_0$ and their crystal residue bases are orthonormal. On every finite label or root component the Gram determinant is a unit of $A_0$, the $A_0$-pairing is perfect and $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. Moreover $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension of the lattice. These are consequences after the grand loop, not prerequisites for it. Only the field-half supplier's inherited AC hypothesis is retained.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A dominant integral weight $\lambda$, the lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ with their residue bases from the grand loop, and the normalised $\sigma$-contravariant forms of [[lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form]] and [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]].

[F1] Grand loop: the pairs $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ and $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ are crystal bases with the partial-inverse and projection clauses C, J, L, N, O and the module/lattice pairing properties; the induced pairing is $A_0$-valued and satisfies $\langle\tilde f_iu,v\rangle\equiv\langle u,\tilde e_iv\rangle\bmod q$ on the lattices ([[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

[F2] The forms: the module form on each finite-dimensional weight space is nondegenerate, the half form is symmetric nondegenerate and integral on the divided lattice, and the large-weight comparison of the half and module pairings has constant term $C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-n_i}\in1+qA_0$ for $\nu=\sum_in_i\alpha_i$; the operator $Q_i$ of the source's Lemma 7.25 is the identity because $a_{ii}=2$ ([[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], [[lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form]]).

[F3] Finite linear algebra over $A_0$: a matrix congruent to the identity modulo $q$ has determinant a unit of $A_0$ and is invertible; over the field the same matrix is invertible, and the inverse pairing matrix identifies the dual lattice with the lattice ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct. Residue orthonormality is an induction on root height using the grand-loop partial inverses; perfection and self-duality follow from a Gram matrix congruent to the identity; the norm criterion follows from positivity of the rational residue form.

1.1 Residue orthonormality. Induct on $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$. For residues $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ choose $i$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$; then $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$ by clause C(r) and J(r), so the adjunction of [F1] gives $\langle b,b'\rangle_0=\langle\tilde e_ib,\tilde e_ib'\rangle_0$. If $\tilde e_ib'=0$ this is $0$; otherwise $\tilde e_ib'$ lies at lower height and, by the lower-height orthonormality and the injectivity of $\tilde e_i$ on the surviving string positions, the pairing is $\delta_{b,b'}$. The top vector has norm $1$, and since all $a_{ii}=2$ the operator $Q_i$ of [F2] is the identity, so no norm larger than $1$ occurs. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Perfection and self-duality. By step 1.1 the Gram matrix of the finite component in the residue basis is congruent to the identity modulo $q$; by [F3] its determinant is a unit of $A_0$ and the matrix is invertible, so the pairing on the finite component is perfect and the dual lattice with respect to the field form equals the lattice itself: $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The negative half. For $U_q^-$ use the corrected degree/colour comparison of [F2] with a sufficiently large regularised dominant weight: $\pi_\lambda$ is a lattice isomorphism on the component and a bijection on its crystal residue sets, and $C_\nu\equiv1\bmod q$; hence the Gram residue of the half lattice is the identity as well, and the same finite-matrix argument gives $A_0$-valuedness, perfection and $\mathcal L(\infty)^\vee=\mathcal L(\infty)$ on each finite component. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 The norm criterion. Suppose $\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0$ but $x$ has a pole in the lattice. Choose the minimal $N>0$ with $q^Nx\in\mathcal L$ and let $\bar x\neq0$ be its residue. In the orthonormal residue basis of step 1.1, $\langle\bar x,\bar x\rangle$ is a sum of squares of rational coordinates, hence a positive rational; on the other hand $q^{2N}\langle x,x\rangle\in qA_0$ has residue $0$, a contradiction. Therefore $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension. [F3, step 1.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Choice. The only choice used is the inherited hypothesis of the negative-half field form, already declared in [F2]; the finite Gram computations and the norm criterion use no further choice. [F2, F3] ∎

[F2] The forms: the module form on each finite-dimensional weight space is nondegenerate, the half form is symmetric nondegenerate and $A$-valued on the word lattice, with the exact $A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ denominator bound on the divided lattice, and the large-weight comparison of the half and module pairings has constant term $C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-n_i}\in1+qA_0$ for $\nu=\sum_in_i\alpha_i$; the operator $Q_i$ of the source's Lemma 7.25 is the identity because $a_{ii}=2$ ([[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], [[lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form]]).

[F3] Finite linear algebra over $A_0$: a matrix congruent to the identity modulo $q$ has determinant a unit of $A_0$ and is invertible; over the field the same matrix is invertible, and the inverse pairing matrix identifies the dual lattice with the lattice ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct. Residue orthonormality is an induction on root height using the grand-loop partial inverses; perfection and self-duality follow from a Gram matrix congruent to the identity; the norm criterion follows from positivity of the rational residue form.

1.1 Residue orthonormality. Induct on $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$. For residues $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ choose $i$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$; then $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$ by clause C(r) and J(r), so the adjunction of [F1] gives $\langle b,b'\rangle_0=\langle\tilde e_ib,\tilde e_ib'\rangle_0$. If $\tilde e_ib'=0$ this is $0$; otherwise $\tilde e_ib'$ lies at lower height and, by the lower-height orthonormality and the injectivity of $\tilde e_i$ on the surviving string positions, the pairing is $\delta_{b,b'}$. The top vector has norm $1$, and since all $a_{ii}=2$ the operator $Q_i$ of [F2] is the identity, so no norm larger than $1$ occurs. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Perfection and self-duality. By step 1.1 the Gram matrix of the finite component in the residue basis is congruent to the identity modulo $q$; by [F3] its determinant is a unit of $A_0$ and the matrix is invertible, so the pairing on the finite component is perfect and the dual lattice with respect to the field form equals the lattice itself: $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. [F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The negative half. For $U_q^-$ use the corrected degree/colour comparison of [F2] with a sufficiently large regularised dominant weight: $\pi_\lambda$ is a lattice isomorphism on the component and a bijection on its crystal residue sets, and $C_\nu\equiv1\bmod q$; hence the Gram residue of the half lattice is the identity as well, and the same finite-matrix argument gives $A_0$-valuedness, perfection and $\mathcal L(\infty)^\vee=\mathcal L(\infty)$ on each finite component. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

4.1 The norm criterion. Suppose $\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0$ but $x$ has a pole in the lattice. Choose the minimal $N>0$ with $q^Nx\in\mathcal L$ and let $\bar x\neq0$ be its residue. In the orthonormal residue basis of step 1.1, $\langle\bar x,\bar x\rangle$ is a sum of squares of rational coordinates, hence a positive rational; on the other hand $q^{2N}\langle x,x\rangle\in qA_0$ has residue $0$, a contradiction. Therefore $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension. [F3, step 1.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Choice. The only choice used is the inherited hypothesis of the negative-half field form, already declared in [F2]; the finite Gram computations and the norm criterion use no further choice. [F2, F3] ∎

## Statement

Let $\star$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear anti-involution of $U_q^-$ fixing each generator $F_i$, so that for a word $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$ one has $(F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r})^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, and let $B$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then $\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution of the Serre quotient, reverses negative words, preserves the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], commutes with the bar involution $\psi$, and preserves $B$: $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$. Consequently $\star$ preserves the crystal lattice $\mathcal L(\infty)$ of [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], the integral residue lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$, and the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-=U_A^-\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ of [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]]. On the integral crystal residue the induced map permutes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. Only this signed lattice preservation is asserted, not an unsigned $\star$-crystal theorem; the sign is what the gluing of the string-ideal global lifts requires.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The negative half $U_q^-$ with generators $F_i$, its divided-power form $U_A^-$, the normalized half form $B$, and the lattices $\mathcal L(\infty),L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)$.

[F1] The word Gram formula and norm characterization ([[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]): $B$ is the symmetric normalized form with $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$; its value on two words is a finite sum over color-matching order-preserving permutations with crossing exponents; $\mathcal L(\infty)=\{P:B(P,P)\in A_0\}=\{P:B(P,U_q^-)\subseteq A_0\}$ and $B$ is positive definite on $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ with orthonormal basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$.

[F2] Integral residues ([[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]]): $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Z[q]$-module whose residue image is $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Zb$, the residue pairing is $\mathbb Z$-valued, and the norm-$1$ elements of $L_{\mathbb Z}$ are exactly the signed basis classes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$ modulo $qL_{\mathbb Z}$.

[F3] Divided-power form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]): $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of the divided powers $F_i^{(r)}$, graded by $-Q_+$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **$\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution.** The assignment $F_i\mapsto F_i$ extended antimultiplicatively is defined on the free algebra, and applying it to a negative Serre relation $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ and reversing the order of each monomial gives $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{r}F_jF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}$, which is the same sum after the substitution $r\mapsto1-a_{ij}-r$ and the exact symmetry $\binom{m}{r}_i=\binom{m}{m-r}_i$ of the Gaussian binomials. Hence $\star$ descends to $U_q^-$, fixes $F_i$, and is an anti-involution: it reverses words and its square is the identity. [F3, algebra]

1.2 **Integral and bar compatibility.** Since $\star$ fixes each divided power $F_i^{(r)}$ (it fixes $F_i$ and the scalar $[r]_i!$), it maps each generator of $U_A^-$ to a generator, so $\star(U_A^-)=U_A^-$. It commutes with $\psi$ because both are $\mathbb Q(q)$-semilinear, $\star$ fixes $q$ while $\psi$ sends $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, and on generators $\psi\star(F_i)=\psi(F_i)=F_i=\star\psi(F_i)$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 **Isometry for the half form.** Write $P=F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$, $Q=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_s}$ as words. Reversing both words, $P^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, $Q^\star=F_{j_s}\cdots F_{j_1}$, and the word Gram formula of [F1] expands both $B(P,Q)$ and $B(P^\star,Q^\star)$ as sums over bijections between matched colors with the same crossing exponents read backwards; reversing a permutation preserves the weight and the crossing number, so the two sums are termwise equal. Hence $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$ on words and, by bilinearity and descent through the Serre ideal, on all of $U_q^-$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Lattice stability.** For $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ one has $B(P^\star,P^\star)=B(P,P)\in A_0$ by step 2.1 and the norm characterization of [F1]; hence $P^\star\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ and $\star$ preserves $\mathcal L(\infty)$. It preserves $U_A^-$ by step 1.2, so it preserves $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$; since it commutes with $\psi$ and $\psi(L_{\mathbb Z})=L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, it also preserves the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1]

4.1 **The signed residue permutation.** For $x\in L_{\mathbb Z}$ with residue $\sum_ba_bb$, the residue of $x^\star$ is $\sum_ba_b'b$ where the coefficients are determined by the orthonormal residue pairing; because the residue pairing is invariant under $\star$ by step 2.1, $a_b'=a_b$ up to the index permutation induced by a signed bijection of the basis: by the signed norm characterization of [F2], if $x$ has norm $1$ then $x^\star$ has norm $1$, so $\star$ maps the set of signed basis classes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$ to itself, permuting it. [F2, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 prove that $\star$ is an anti-involution preserving $U_A^-$ and commuting with bar, step 2.1 proves that it is an isometry of the normalized half form, step 3.1 proves preservation of $\mathcal L(\infty)$, $L_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, and step 4.1 gives the signed permutation of the integral crystal residue. No unsigned star-crystal theorem is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $i\in I$ and let $e_i'$ be the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with string decomposition $u=\sum_lF_i^{(l)}u_l$, $u_l\in\ker e_i'$ ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]).

(i) If $u\in U_A^-$ then all $u_l$ lie in $U_A^-$. The integral projector is
$$P_i=\sum_l(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}(e_i')^l,\qquad u_l=q_i^{l(l-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^lu,$$
where all powers of $e_i'$ are ordinary powers, not divided by $[l]_i!$.

(ii) Define
$$I_{(i,n)}^A:=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-=\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}\bigl(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-,$$
$$J_{(i,n)}^A:=\pi_\lambda\bigl(I_{(i,n)}^A\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda),$$
with $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ as in [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]]. The latter is an $A$-submodule inside the field string-image subspace $F_i^nV(\lambda)$, not a $U_q$-submodule or a $U_A$-stable lattice in general; its equality with $V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed here.

(iii) The integral residue of $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is the free $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$, and the corresponding rational residue of $F_i^nU_q^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is its $\mathbb Q$-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple of $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is a conclusion of the subsequent string-ideal induction, not an input.

(iv) On every $U_A$-stable integrable module lattice $M_A$, if a label $\mu$ satisfies $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=-n\le-1$, then every $u\in(M_A)_\mu$ satisfies the finite identity
$$u=\sum_{k\ge n}(-1)^{k-n}\binom{k-1}{k-n}_iF_i^{(k)}E_i^{(k)}u,$$
and consequently $(M_A)_\mu=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k)}(M_A)_{\mu+k\alpha_i}$. This is the exact boundary generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The negative half with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$, the divided-power form $U_A^-$, the crystal lattice $\mathcal L(\infty)$ with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and the integral residue lattice of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]].

[F1] Integral string coefficients ([[lem-divided-power-half-has-integral-skew-string-coefficients]]): the string decomposition coefficients of $u\in U_A^-$ are integral: $u_l\in U_A^-$, $P_i``(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$, and both $e_i'$ and its conjugate preserve $U_A^-$.

[F2] Unique string decomposition ([[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]]): every $u\in U_q^-$ has a unique finite decomposition $u=\sum_lF_i^{(l)}u_l$ with $u_l\in\ker e_i'$; for $u\in F_i^nU_q^-$ one has $u_l=0$ for $l<n$, and conversely.

[F3] Crystal and projection compatibility ([[thm-crystal-basis-of-the-negative-half]], [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]]): $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$, $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ act on $\mathcal B(\infty)$ as the crystal operators, and the highest-weight projection is compatible with the crystal operators modulo $q$.

## Statement

Let $D$ be the normalized Drinfeld pairing of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]], $D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y)$ on $U_q^+[\nu]\times U_q^-[-\nu]$, where $B_K$ is the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then:

(i) $D$ is homogeneous, descends to the actual Serre quotients $U_q^\pm$, and is nondegenerate (equivalently perfect) over $\mathbb Q(q)$ in every finite root degree; its rank-one values are $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$.

(ii) $D$ equals the formal generic Hopf pairing on the simple-root Borel extensions with the exact generator and toral normalization, so that
$$D(xx',y)=\sum D(x,y_{(1)})D(x',y_{(2)}),\qquad D(x,yy')=\sum D(x_{(1)},y)D(x_{(2)},y'),$$
with $\Delta y$ on the negative Borel and $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}x$ on the positive Borel, including their toral factors.

These are field identities; no divided-power integral perfectness and no $A$-valuedness of $D$ is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The normalized half form $B_K$ on $U_q^-$, the isomorphism $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$, $E_i\mapsto F_i$, the degree scalar $d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}$, and the generic Hopf pairing between the Serre halves.

[F1] Half form perfectness and values ([[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]]): $B_K$ is the unique normalized homogeneous form on $U_q^-$ with $B_K(F_iP,Q)=B_K(P,e_i'Q)$; it is nondegenerate on each finite-dimensional $U_q^-[-\nu]$; and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ with $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$.

[F2] Generic Hopf pairing ([[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]]): the formal quantum Serre halves carry a nondegenerate pairing $(x,y)$ determined by the coproduct adjunction identities, with the mixed generator values $\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ and the prescribed toral values.

[F3] Coproduct and skew recursion ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]], [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]): $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, and the normalized half form satisfies the degree-shifted recursion $B_K(F_iP,Q)=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}B_K(P,e_i'Q)$ in the form dictionary, equivalently the generator and toral normalization fixed in [F1].

[F4] Divided-power form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]): the halves are root-graded and the divided powers $E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)}$ are the homogeneous generators used in the rank-one checks.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Transport makes $D$ homogeneous and perfect.** By [F1] the form $B_K$ is nondegenerate on each finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$, and $\iota$ restricts to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear isomorphism $U_q^+[\nu]\to U_q^-[-\nu]$; multiplying by the nonzero scalar $d_\nu^{-1}$ does not change nondegeneracy. Hence $D$ is a homogeneous bilinear pairing perfect on every finite root degree, and its generator values are those displayed in [F1] and the Statement. [F1, F4]

1.2 **Descent to the Serre quotients.** The half form $B_K$ is defined on the actual Serre quotient by [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and is nondegenerate there; since $\iota$ identifies the positive Serre quotient with the negative one by the presentation comparison of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]], the transport $D$ is defined on the quotient of each half and introduces no free-word radical. [F1, F3]

1.3 **The generic pairing equals $D$.** By [F2] the formal generic pairing is determined by the adjunction identities together with its values on generators and toral directions. ## Statement

Let $D$ be the normalized Drinfeld pairing of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]], $D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y)$ on $U_q^+[\nu]\times U_q^-[-\nu]$, where $B_K$ is the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then:

(i) $D$ is homogeneous, descends to the actual Serre quotients $U_q^\pm$, and is nondegenerate (equivalently perfect) over $\mathbb Q(q)$ in every finite root degree; its rank-one values are $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$.

(ii) $D$ equals the formal generic Hopf pairing on the simple-root Borel extensions with the exact generator and toral normalization, so that
$$D(xx',y)=\sum D(x,y_{(1)})D(x',y_{(2)}),\qquad D(x,yy')=\sum D(x_{(1)},y)D(x_{(2)},y'),$$
with $\Delta y$ on the negative Borel and $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}x$ on the positive Borel, including their toral factors.

These are field identities; no divided-power integral perfectness and no $A$-valuedness of $D$ is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The normalized half form $B_K$ on $U_q^-$, the isomorphism $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$, $E_i\mapsto F_i$, the degree scalar $d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}$, and the generic Hopf pairing between the Serre halves.

[F1] Half form perfectness and values ([[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]]): $B_K$ is the unique normalized homogeneous form on $U_q^-$ with $B_K(F_iP,Q)=B_K(P,e_i'Q)$; it is nondegenerate on each finite-dimensional $U_q^-[-\nu]$; and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ with $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$.

[F2] Generic Hopf pairing ([[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]]): the formal quantum Serre halves carry a nondegenerate pairing $(x,y)$ determined by the coproduct adjunction identities, with the mixed generator values $\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ and the prescribed toral values.

[F3] Coproduct and skew recursion ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]], [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]): $\Delta E_i=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, and the normalized half form satisfies the degree-shifted recursion $B_K(F_iP,Q)=B_K(P,e_i'Q)$ in the form dictionary, equivalently the generator and toral normalization fixed in [F1].

[F4] Divided-power form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]): the halves are root-graded and the divided powers $E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)}$ are the homogeneous generators used in the rank-one checks.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Transport makes $D$ homogeneous and perfect.** By [F1] the form $B_K$ is nondegenerate on each finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$, and $\iota$ restricts to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear isomorphism $U_q^+[\nu]\to U_q^-[-\nu]$; multiplying by the nonzero scalar $d_\nu^{-1}$ does not change nondegeneracy. Hence $D$ is a homogeneous bilinear pairing perfect on every finite root degree, and its generator values are those displayed in [F1] and the Statement. [F1, F4]

1.2 **Descent to the Serre quotients.** The half form $B_K$ is defined on the actual Serre quotient by [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and is nondegenerate there; since $\iota$ identifies the positive Serre quotient with the negative one by the presentation comparison of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]], the transport $D$ is defined on the quotient of each half and introduces no free-word radical. [F1, F3]

1.3 **The generic pairing equals $D$.** By [F2] the formal generic pairing is determined by the adjunction identities together with its values on generators and toral directions. Extracting one $E_i$ (respectively $F_i$) from $\Delta y$ (respectively $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}x$) in the adjunction identity and comparing with the recursion of [F3] shows that the generic pairing satisfies the same normalized skew recursion as $B_K$ with degree factor $d_\nu/d_{\nu-\alpha_i}=q_i-q_i^{-1}$; a word-height induction on the negative half, using the coproduct formulas of [F3] and the toral factor retention in [F2], therefore identifies the two pairings on the simple-root Borel extensions, including their toral factors. Hence the two adjunction identities displayed in the Statement hold for $D$. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 **Toral convention and limits of the claim.** The toral normalization is fixed by the root bilinear form and the counit exactly as in [F2]; the verification above uses the coproduct on the negative Borel and the opposite coproduct on the positive Borel, as required by the tensor orientation. Since all computations are performed in the field $\mathbb Q(q)$ with the finite graded pieces of [F1] and no lattice freeness is used, no integral perfectness or $A$-valuedness is obtained. [F2, step 1.3]

3.1 **Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 give (i), step 2.1 gives (ii), and step 2.1 records the exact field-level scope; in particular the rank-one values carry the factor $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-n}$ and no lower-lattice integrality is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $\Theta=\sum_{\nu\in Q_+}\Theta_\nu\in\widehat C$ be the $D$-coevaluation family of the diagonal root-height completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], built from the normalized Drinfeld pairing $D$ of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]] and its homogeneous dual bases ([[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]], [[lem-the-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-is-nondegenerate-in-each-root-degree]]). Then $\Theta$ is the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner for the library coproduct $\Delta$: that is,
$$\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\,\overline\Delta(u)\qquad\text{for all }u\in U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad \overline\Delta(u)=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u)),$$
among families with $\Theta_0=1$. Its generator recursions are
$$[1\otimes E_i,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(E_i\otimes K_i)-(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i},$$
$$[F_i\otimes1,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(K_i^{-1}\otimes F_i)-(K_i\otimes F_i)\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i},$$
where components of negative root degree are $0$ and the toral parts commute because $\Theta_\nu$ has toral weight zero. In rank one, $\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)}$ with $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$, so that $\Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})E_i\otimes F_i$. The family evaluates precisely under the explicit finite-support hypotheses of the completion. This is not the native unscaled doubled-torus $\Psi\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ relation, and no integral algebra coefficient claim is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ with coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]], the fixed $\mathbb Q$-linear automorphism $\psi$ with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$ ([[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]), the resulting $\overline\Delta(u)=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, the diagonal root-height completion $\widehat C$ with $\Theta_0=1$ and its finite-support action of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], and the normalized pairing $D$ of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]].

[F1] Dual-basis sums ([[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]]): for each $\nu$ the element $\Theta_\nu=\sum_au_a\otimes v^a$ over any homogeneous basis $(u_a)$ of $U_q^+[\nu]$ with $D$-dual basis $(v^a)$ is independent of the choice, is a finite $\mathbb Q$-linear combination of the tensor product $U_q^+[\nu]\otimes U_q^-[-\nu]$, and $\Theta_0=1$; the family acts vectorwise finitely exactly under the completion's hypotheses.

[F2] Perfect graded pairing ([[lem-the-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-is-nondegenerate-in-each-root-degree]]): $D$ is homogeneous, perfect on every finite root degree, and satisfies the Hopf adjunctions
$$D(x,yy')=\sum D(x_{(1)},y)D(x_{(2)},y'),\qquad D(xx',y)=\sum D(x,y_{(1)})D(x',y_{(2)})$$
for the library coproduct on $U_q^-$ and the opposite coproduct on $U_q^+$ ([[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]]), together with the normalization $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$. On the toral directions $D(K_\nu,K_\mu)=q^{(\nu,\mu)}$.

[F3] Presentation transport ([[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]): the semilinear involution $\varphi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h)=K_{-h}$ carries Lusztig's source coproduct $\Delta_L$ and source form $B_L$ to the library coproduct and normalized form up to the tensor flip; the source coefficient $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation equals $d_\nu$ times the $B_K$-coevaluation exactly. The comparison maps in the completed tensor square are coefficientwise isomorphisms on homogeneous components.

[F4] Skew derivations and separation ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[lem-the-negative-half-is-separated-by-iterated-skew-derivations]]): the Serre presentation of $U_q^-$ defines left and right skew derivations $e_i'$, $e_i''$ with $e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+xe_i''(y)$ and the quotient rule for the toral numerators; and for every nonzero positive-height element of $U_q^+$ some iterated skew derivative is nonzero, so a positive-degree half element all of whose iterated derivatives vanish is zero.

[F5] Hopf identities ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]): $\Delta,\overline\Delta$ are algebra homomorphisms; $\overline\Delta(u)=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$ is compatible with the algebra structure and $\overline\Delta\equiv\Delta$ on the toral subalgebra; $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, so $\overline\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i+1\otimes E_i$ and $\overline\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i^{-1}\otimes F_i$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The candidate family.** Define $\Theta_\nu$ by [F1] and put $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu\in\widehat C$; then $\Theta_0=1$ and, by [F1], the family is independent of all choices of bases and acts vectorwise finitely under the completion's hypotheses. Its components are toral weight zero, because each $\Theta_\nu$ pairs the root degrees $\nu$ and $-\nu$. [F1]

1.2 **The $E_i$-identity in the pairing picture.** Expand all tensors in homogeneous $D$-dual bases and test $\Delta(E_i)\Theta_\nu=\Theta_{\nu+?}\overline\Delta(E_i)$ coefficientwise. By [F1] and [F2] the positive tensor factor of $\Theta_\nu$ can be paired with an arbitrary element $x$ of $U_q^+[\nu]$; writing the resulting linear functional as $D$-duality turns the equation into the two adjunction identities of [F2] evaluated on $xy$ versus the skew-derivation decomposition of the products $E_ix$ and $xE_i$ in the halves. Concretely, moving $E_i$ across the first tensor factor produces the denominators $(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ of the presentation and the toral numerators $K_i^{\pm1}$ of [F4]; comparing the two sides degree by degree gives exactly $$[1\otimes E_i,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(E_i\otimes K_i)-(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i},$$ with the convention that $\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}=0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. [F1, F2, F4, F5]

2.1 **Generator identities: toral case and structure of the verification.** For $u=K_h$ both $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$ and $\overline\Delta(K_h)=(\psi\otimes\psi)(K_{-h}\otimes K_{-h})=K_h\otimes K_h$, and $\Theta_\nu$ commutes with $K_h\otimes1$ and $1\otimes K_h$ by toral weight zero, so $\Delta(K_h)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(K_h)$. Since $\Delta$ and $\overline\Delta$ are algebra homomorphisms [F5], once the two root-generator identities hold, the identity extends to all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. [F5, step 1.1]

3.1 **The $F_i$-identity.** The same coefficientwise computation with $F_i$ in the second tensor factor, using the adjunction with the opposite coproduct and the right skew derivation of [F4], yields $$[F_i\otimes1,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(K_i^{-1}\otimes F_i)-(K_i\otimes F_i)\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}.$$ Both displayed recursions determine $\Theta_\nu$ from the components of lower degree, and in particular the first-degree component is forced by $D(E_i,F_i)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and $D(1,1)=1$. Since these recursions are equivalent to the two generator identities, $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$ holds on generators and hence on all $u$ by step 2.1. [F2, F4, step 1.2]

4.1 **Uniqueness.** Let $\Theta,\Theta'$ be two normalized solutions and $\Omega=\Theta-\Theta'$, so $\Omega\in\widehat C$, $\Omega_0=0$, and $\Delta(u)\Omega=\Omega\overline\Delta(u)$ for all $u$. Suppose $\Omega\ne0$ and let $\nu_0$ be a minimal root degree with $\Omega_{\nu_0}\ne0$; by minimality the $\alpha_i$-recursions of step 3.1 applied to $\Omega$ carry no lower-degree terms, so for every $i$ the skew derivatives of the two coefficient tensors of $\Omega_{\nu_0}$ vanish, in the sense of the two recursions. Expanding $\Omega_{\nu_0}$ in homogeneous bases of $U_q^+[\nu_0]$ and testing against $D$-dual vectors, the two recursions and [F2] turn the generator identities into the statement that all iterated skew derivatives of every coefficient vector in the positive half vanish; the separation theorem [F4] then forces every coefficient of $\Omega_{\nu_0}$ to be zero, a contradiction. Hence $\Omega=0$ and the normalized solution is unique. [F1, F2, F4, step 3.1]

5.1 **Rank-one coefficient.** Let $I=\{i\}$. Since the degree-$n\alpha_i$ component of $U_q^+$ with its basis element $E_i^{(n)}$ pairs with $F_i^{(n)}$ by [F2] with value $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$, the inverse coefficient is $$\bigl(D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})\bigr)^{-1}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^nq_i^{n(n-1)/2}[n]_i!=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!,$$ using $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}[n]_i!$. Hence $\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)}$, and for $n=1$ this is $\Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})E_i\otimes F_i$. [F2, step 4.1]

6.1 **Conclusion and scope.** Steps 1.1–3.1 construct the normalized family and the two generator recursions; step 4.1 proves uniqueness by minimal degree and separation; step 5.1 computes the rank-one coefficient. The construction used only the graded pairing, the completion's finite-support hypotheses and the presentation's skew derivations, so the family is the $D$-coevaluation of the completion and not the unscaled doubled-torus normalization as recorded by the transport dictionary of [F3]; no integrality of coefficients was asserted at any point. [F3, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $\Theta=\sum_{\nu\in Q_+}\Theta_\nu\in\widehat C$ be the $D$-coevaluation family of the diagonal root-height completion $\widehat C$ of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], built from the normalized Drinfeld pairing $D$ of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]] and its homogeneous dual bases ([[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]], [[lem-the-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-is-nondegenerate-in-each-root-degree]]). Then $\Theta$ is the unique normalized bar-coproduct intertwiner for the library coproduct $\Delta$: that is,
$$\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\,\overline\Delta(u)\qquad\text{for all }u\in U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad \overline\Delta(u)=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u)),$$
among families with $\Theta_0=1$. Its generator recursions are
$$[1\otimes E_i,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(E_i\otimes K_i)-(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i},$$
$$[F_i\otimes1,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(K_i^{-1}\otimes F_i)-(K_i\otimes F_i)\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i},$$
where components of negative root degree are $0$ and the toral parts commute because $\Theta_\nu$ has toral weight zero. In rank one, $\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)}$ with $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$, so that $\Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})E_i\otimes F_i$. The family evaluates precisely under the explicit finite-support hypotheses of the completion. This is not the native unscaled doubled-torus $\Psi\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ relation, and no integral algebra coefficient claim is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ with coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]], the fixed $\mathbb Q$-linear automorphism $\psi$ with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$ ([[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]), the resulting $\overline\Delta(u)=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, the diagonal root-height completion $\widehat C$ with $\Theta_0=1$ and its finite-support action of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]], and the normalized pairing $D$ of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]].

[F1] Dual-basis sums ([[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]]): for each $\nu$ the element $\Theta_\nu=\sum_au_a\otimes v^a$ over any homogeneous basis $(u_a)$ of $U_q^+[\nu]$ with $D$-dual basis $(v^a)$ is independent of the choice, is a finite $\mathbb Q$-linear combination of the tensor product $U_q^+[\nu]\otimes U_q^-[-\nu]$, and $\Theta_0=1$; the family acts vectorwise finitely exactly under the completion's hypotheses.

[F2] Perfect graded pairing ([[lem-the-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-is-nondegenerate-in-each-root-degree]]): $D$ is homogeneous, perfect on every finite root degree, and satisfies the Hopf adjunctions
$$D(x,yy')=\sum D(x_{(1)},y)D(x_{(2)},y'),\qquad D(xx',y)=\sum D(x,y_{(1)})D(x',y_{(2)})$$
for the library coproduct on $U_q^-$ and the opposite coproduct on $U_q^+$ ([[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]]), together with the normalization $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$. On the toral directions $D(K_\nu,K_\mu)=q^{(\nu,\mu)}$.

[F3] Presentation transport ([[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]): the semilinear involution $\varphi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h)=K_{-h}$ carries Lusztig's source coproduct $\Delta_L$ and source form $B_L$ to the library coproduct and normalized form up to the tensor flip; the source coefficient $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation equals $d_\nu$ times the $B_K$-coevaluation exactly. The comparison maps in the completed tensor square are coefficientwise isomorphisms on homogeneous components.

[F4] Skew derivations and separation ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[lem-the-negative-half-is-separated-by-iterated-skew-derivations]]): the Serre presentation of $U_q^-$ defines left and right skew derivations $e_i'$, $e_i''$ with $e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}xe_i'(y)$ for homogeneous $x$, with the opposite twist for $e_i''$ and the quotient rule for the toral numerators; and for every nonzero positive-height element of $U_q^+$ some iterated skew derivative is nonzero, so a positive-degree half element all of whose iterated derivatives vanish is zero.

[F5] Hopf identities ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]): $\Delta,\overline\Delta$ are algebra homomorphisms; $\overline\Delta(u)=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$ is compatible with the algebra structure and $\overline\Delta\equiv\Delta$ on the toral subalgebra; $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$, so $\overline\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i+1\otimes E_i$ and $\overline\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i^{-1}\otimes F_i$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The candidate family.** Define $\Theta_\nu$ by [F1] and put $\Theta=\sum_\nu\Theta_\nu\in\widehat C$; then $\Theta_0=1$ and, by [F1], the family is independent of all choices of bases and acts vectorwise finitely under the completion's hypotheses. Its components are toral weight zero, because each $\Theta_\nu$ pairs the root degrees $\nu$ and $-\nu$. [F1]

1.2 **The $E_i$-identity in the pairing picture.** Expand all tensors in homogeneous $D$-dual bases and test $\Delta(E_i)\Theta_\nu=\Theta_{\nu+?}\overline\Delta(E_i)$ coefficientwise. By [F1] and [F2] the positive tensor factor of $\Theta_\nu$ can be paired with an arbitrary element $x$ of $U_q^+[\nu]$; writing the resulting linear functional as $D$-duality turns the equation into the two adjunction identities of [F2] evaluated on $xy$ versus the skew-derivation decomposition of the products $E_ix$ and $xE_i$ in the halves. Concretely, moving $E_i$ across the first tensor factor produces the denominators $(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ of the presentation and the toral numerators $K_i^{\pm1}$ of [F4]; comparing the two sides degree by degree gives exactly $$[1\otimes E_i,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(E_i\otimes K_i)-(E_i\otimes K_i^{-1})\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i},$$ with the convention that $\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}=0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. [F1, F2, F4, F5]

2.1 **Generator identities: toral case and structure of the verification.** For $u=K_h$ both $\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h$ and $\overline\Delta(K_h)=(\psi\otimes\psi)(K_{-h}\otimes K_{-h})=K_h\otimes K_h$, and $\Theta_\nu$ commutes with $K_h\otimes1$ and $1\otimes K_h$ by toral weight zero, so $\Delta(K_h)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(K_h)$. Since $\Delta$ and $\overline\Delta$ are algebra homomorphisms [F5], once the two root-generator identities hold, the identity extends to all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. [F5, step 1.1]

3.1 **The $F_i$-identity.** The same coefficientwise computation with $F_i$ in the second tensor factor, using the adjunction with the opposite coproduct and the right skew derivation of [F4], yields $$[F_i\otimes1,\Theta_\nu]=\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}(K_i^{-1}\otimes F_i)-(K_i\otimes F_i)\Theta_{\nu-\alpha_i}.$$ Both displayed recursions determine $\Theta_\nu$ from the components of lower degree, and in particular the first-degree component is forced by $D(E_i,F_i)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and $D(1,1)=1$. Since these recursions are equivalent to the two generator identities, $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$ holds on generators and hence on all $u$ by step 2.1. [F2, F4, step 1.2]

4.1 **Uniqueness.** Let $\Theta,\Theta'$ be two normalized solutions and $\Omega=\Theta-\Theta'$, so $\Omega\in\widehat C$, $\Omega_0=0$, and $\Delta(u)\Omega=\Omega\overline\Delta(u)$ for all $u$. Suppose $\Omega\ne0$ and let $\nu_0$ be a minimal root degree with $\Omega_{\nu_0}\ne0$; by minimality the $\alpha_i$-recursions of step 3.1 applied to $\Omega$ carry no lower-degree terms, so for every $i$ the skew derivatives of the two coefficient tensors of $\Omega_{\nu_0}$ vanish, in the sense of the two recursions. Expanding $\Omega_{\nu_0}$ in homogeneous bases of $U_q^+[\nu_0]$ and testing against $D$-dual vectors, the two recursions and [F2] turn the generator identities into the statement that all iterated skew derivatives of every coefficient vector in the positive half vanish; the separation theorem [F4] then forces every coefficient of $\Omega_{\nu_0}$ to be zero, a contradiction. Hence $\Omega=0$ and the normalized solution is unique. [F1, F2, F4, step 3.1]

5.1 **Rank-one coefficient.** Let $I=\{i\}$. Since the degree-$n\alpha_i$ component of $U_q^+$ with its basis element $E_i^{(n)}$ pairs with $F_i^{(n)}$ by [F2] with value $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$, the inverse coefficient is $$\bigl(D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})\bigr)^{-1}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^nq_i^{n(n-1)/2}[n]_i!=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!,$$ using $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}[n]_i!$. Hence $\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)}$, and for $n=1$ this is $\Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})E_i\otimes F_i$. [F2, step 4.1]

6.1 **Conclusion and scope.** Steps 1.1–3.1 construct the normalized family and the two generator recursions; step 4.1 proves uniqueness by minimal degree and separation; step 5.1 computes the rank-one coefficient. The construction used only the graded pairing, the completion's finite-support hypotheses and the presentation's skew derivations, so the family is the $D$-coevaluation of the completion and not the unscaled doubled-torus normalization as recorded by the transport dictionary of [F3]; no integrality of coefficients was asserted at any point. [F3, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎
